Funds:
Response = National/State Disaster Response Fund

⚠ Trap: NDRF is both the Force and the Fund (acronym trap)

# DM plans and the DM (Amendment) Act 2025 → provisions
Plan / Act | Section / year | Provision

Modern view: Phases = overlapping continuum, not a line

# Safety drills, awareness and community-based DRR

Severe-weather forecasts improved 40-50%

# Technology in DM → tools and terms
## 1. GIS and remote sensing
GIS | Stores, analyses and overlays remote-sensed and spatial data; key use = hazard mapping (earthquake, landslide, flood, fire); analyses flood patterns and topography → proactive action (APPSC 2025 key)
Remote sensing (aerial and satellite) | Fast, synoptic view of large areas; uses: inundation mapping, damage assessment, flood-hazard zoning, drought early warning
Google Earth Engine | Cloud platform processing large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping
ISRO Disaster Management Support Programme | Covers floods, cyclones, droughts, forest fires, landslides, earthquakes
NDEM (National Database for Emergency Management) | GIS repository for the whole DM cycle, maintained by ISRO
CAP (Common Alerting Protocol) | Integrates public warnings

# Disaster management cycle — phases
Disaster management has four phases
Phase | When | Aim | Includes
Prevention | Before a disaster | Stop a hazard from becoming a disaster — proactive and long-term | Land-use zoning; regulating deforestation; controlling industrial siting
Mitigation | Before a disaster | Reduce disaster risk and the severity / impact; minimise future losses — the most cost-effective phase | Earthquake-resistant buildings, embankments, building codes, afforestation, insurance, hazard mapping
Preparedness / preparation | Before a disaster | Readiness — ensures a ready and effective response; capacity building; the first and critical step | Preparedness planning, (Early) Warning Systems, evacuation arrangements, community preparedness, emergency resources, coordination, mock drills, stockpiling, training through Aapda Mitra, Emergency Operation Centres, contingency plans
Response | During or immediately / just after | Immediate action — save lives; meet basic needs; time-critical | Search and rescue, evacuation, first aid, temporary shelters, food and water, law and order
Recovery | After a disaster | Restore normal life / normalcy; reduce future vulnerability; Build Back Better — long-term; builds resilience | Rehabilitation, reconstruction, livelihood support, psycho-social care, resilient infrastructure
Prep additions by phase: Prevention/Mitigation - retrofitting, land-use planning; Preparedness - DM plans, training responders (Aapda Mitra), stockpiles, early warning (CAP-SACHET); Response - search and rescue (NDRF, armed forces), shelter, food, medical aid, psychological support, restoring critical services; Recovery and Reconstruction - damage assessment, compensation, livelihoods, "Build Back Better", psycho-social care
Prep merges Prevention/Mitigation into one phase; Response = During (some notes: Post-disaster)
Risk assessment leads to mitigation
Non-structural mitigation: Community awareness and education programmes
Cyclone mitigation: Planting trees along coastal areas; earthquake mitigation: reframing and implementing building-construction guidelines

State category | Centre : State

Pre-disaster — prevention, mitigation, preparedness; response during; recovery post-disaster

Phase | Measures

system.text:
You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

content.text:
STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves and Conservation Reserves

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Wildlife Protection Act 1972 – Protected Area Categories
First comprehensive wildlife law of India; Presidential assent 9 September 1972.
PAs under it: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Conservation Reserves, Community Reserves.
Category | Declared by / on | Rights and use
National Park | State (or Centre) | Highest protection; no grazing or private rights
Wildlife Sanctuary | State | Some activities/rights regulated but allowed
Conservation Reserve (Sec 36A) | State, on government-owned land beside or linking PAs, after consulting locals | Local rights unaffected; committees with panchayats
Community Reserve | State, on private/community land freely offered | Rights unaffected; land cannot be inside an NP, WLS or CR
Conservation and community reserves were added by the WPA (Amendment) 2002.
Supreme Court: 10-km mining buffer extended to all wetland conservation reserves; ordinary eco-sensitive buffer around NPs/WLS = 1 km. Final ESZ notifications: 353.
# Protected Area Counts
Category | Count (2026)
National Parks | 109 (44,374 sq km)
Wildlife Sanctuaries | 573 (1,22,420 sq km)
Conservation Reserves | 127
Community Reserves | 75
Tiger Reserves | 58 – 84,488 sq km (~2.6% of India, 29 Jul 2026)
Elephant Reserves | 33
Biosphere Reserves | 18
PA network ≈ 5.3% of India's geographical area; NPs alone ≈ 1.35%.
Most national parks: Madhya Pradesh (11 in a PYQ key), followed by Andaman & Nicobar; Assam has 7. Maharashtra – most wildlife sanctuaries.
Bhutan – more than 30% of its area under national parks.
# Firsts and Superlatives
FIRST / superlative | Fact
First NP (India and mainland Asia) | Jim Corbett, Uttarakhand – 1936 as Hailey NP; Project Tiger launched there 1973
First bird sanctuary | Vedanthangal (Tamil Nadu)
First wolf sanctuary | Mahuadanr, Latehar, Jharkhand
First BR | Nilgiri (1986)
First high-altitude cold desert BR in WNBR | Cold Desert, HP (2025)
Largest BRs | Great Rann of Kutch (12,454 sq km) > Gulf of Mannar (10,500) > Sundarbans (9,630)
Smallest BR | Dibru-Saikhowa (765 sq km)
Largest high-altitude PA | Tsarap Chu (Spiti, HP) – HP's 5th conservation reserve
First NP with a mascot | Kanha – "Bhoorsingh the Barasingha"
World's first NP | Yellowstone (1872)
Canada's first NP | Banff (1885)
Other firsts: International Solar Alliance – first treaty-based intergovernmental body headquartered in India (Paris 2015; Secretariat Gurugram); FRI Dehradun – roots in the Imperial FRI (1906); Montreal Protocol – adopted 1987, in force 1989 (ozone).
# National Parks → State
State / UT | National parks
Andhra Pradesh | Sri Venkateswara, Papikonda, Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram)
Arunachal | Namdapha, Mouling (not Assam)
Assam | Kaziranga (one-horned rhino), Manas, Orang, Nameri
Madhya Pradesh | Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura, Madhav
Rajasthan | Ranthambore, Keoladeo (Bharatpur), Sariska (Alwar)
Gujarat | Gir (Junagadh) – Asiatic lion
Karnataka | Nagarhole, Bandipur
Kerala | Silent Valley (Palakkad, Malappuram), Periyar
Uttarakhand | Nanda Devi, Valley of Flowers, Jim Corbett, Rajaji
West Bengal | Sundarbans, Neora Valley (Kalimpong)
Maharashtra | Tadoba, Gugamal
Uttar Pradesh | Dudhwa (Lakhimpur Kheri)
Bihar / Jharkhand | Valmiki (West Champaran) / Betla
Goa / HP / Sikkim | Mollem / Great Himalayan (Kullu) / Khangchendzonga
Meghalaya | Nokrek (Garo Hills, not Khasi), Balpakram (not Manipur)
Manipur | Keibul Lamjao – floating park on Loktak (phumdis), Bishnupur
Ladakh / J&K | Hemis / Dachigam, Salim Ali NP (Srinagar)
Chhattisgarh / Odisha | Indravati (Bastar) / Similipal (Mayurbhanj; not MP)
Nagaland / Tamil Nadu | Intanki (Ntangki) / Guindy (Chennai, not Kerala)
Mizoram | Phawngpul (Blue Mountain, Lawngtlai)
A&N | Campbell Bay (Great Nicobar), Rani Jhansi Marine NP (1996, 320.06 sq km)
# National Parks – Landscape, Rivers and Features
Park | Landscape / feature
Corbett | Shivalik and Himalayan foothills; Ramganga, Kosi (not Ganga)
Kaziranga | Brahmaputra, Diphlu (not Manas); TR 2007
Silent Valley | Nilgiri Hills, W Ghats; Kunthipuzha (not Kaveri; not Nallamalai)
Ranthambore / Sariska | Aravalli–Vindhyan / Aravalli dry forest; tigress Machhali (T-16) died 18 Aug 2016
Tadoba–Andhari | Chandrapur; Deccan/central Indian dry deciduous; one of the oldest TRs
Keoladeo (Ghana) | Former Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary; NP 1981, WHS 1985; Ramsar
Dudhwa | Terai grassland, swamp deer; rhino rehabilitation from Assam, 1984
Pench | MP + Maharashtra; inspired Kipling's The Jungle Book
Neora Valley | Eastern Himalayan forest
Campbell Bay | Tropical evergreen island forest
Kanha (1955) | Hard-ground Barasingha; core of Kanha TR (1973–74); Green Guard Award 2001–02
Satpura | Dhoopgarh peak; Narmadapuram; ~524 sq km, 1981
Namdapha | Tropical to arctic climate; Dapha bum (Mishmi) – Patkai; Noa Dihing; largest PA of the E Himalaya hotspot
Valley of Flowers | Wholly temperate alpine; Chamoli; 87 sq km
Nanda Devi | 7,817 m, 4th highest peak of India
Indravati | Wild buffalo; NP 1981, TR 1983
Papikonda | Godavari flows through it; 1,012.86 sq km, NP 2008; tiger "Explorer" from Tadoba released (14 Feb 2026)
Similipal / Periyar | Eastern Ghats / Western Ghats (tigers, elephants – not hangul)
Intanki | Ten captive-bred Asian Giant Tortoises released
Rajaji became India's 48th TR (2015); Orang 49th.
# Species → Protected-area Habitat
Species | Habitat
Musk deer | Kedarnath and Askot WLS (Uttarakhand)
Great Indian Bustard | Desert NP (Rajasthan); Rollapadu WLS (AP); < 150 birds; 2024 SC order on underground power lines
Hangul (Kashmir stag) | Dachigam (near Srinagar, Zabarwan Range)
Barasingha | Kanha – state animal of MP
Snow leopard | Cold Desert BR, Kibber
Asiatic lion | Gir; Kuno Palpur proposed as second home – Gujarat refused until 33 IUCN studies
One-horned rhino | Kaziranga
# Wildlife Sanctuaries → State/district
Sanctuary | State (district)
Askot | Uttarakhand (Pithoragarh)
Binsar | Uttarakhand (Almora)
Mahuadanr | Jharkhand (Latehar) – wolf
Sitanadi | Chhattisgarh – mainly Sal
Pitti | Lakshadweep – bird sanctuary
Nelapattu | AP – smallest WLS in AP
Kedarnath | Uttarakhand – musk deer
# Biosphere Reserves
## Order of Establishment
Year | BRs
1986 | Nilgiri (first)
1988 | Nanda Devi, Nokrek
1989 | Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Manas, Great Nicobar
1999 | Pachmarhi
## UNESCO MAB (World Network) Status
18 BRs in India; 13 in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Listed examples: Nilgiri (2000, first), Gulf of Mannar (2001), Sundarbans (2001), Nanda Devi (2004), Agasthyamalai (2016), Khangchendzonga (2018), Panna (2020), Cold Desert (Sep 2025, latest).
Kachchh (largest) is not in the World Network.
Agasthyamalai: TN eviction notices after A. John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu (2025) – tribal-rights concerns.
AP: Seshachalam BR (4,755.997 sq km).
# Natural World Heritage Sites of India
Site | State | Year
Kaziranga NP | Assam | 1985
Keoladeo NP | Rajasthan | 1985
Manas WLS | Assam | 1985
Sundarbans NP | West Bengal | 1987
Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers NPs | Uttarakhand | 1988 (extended 2005)
Western Ghats | 6 states (39 sites in 4 states) | 2012
Great Himalayan NP | Kullu, HP (754.4 sq km) | June 2014
Khangchendzonga NP (mixed) | Sikkim | 2016
# World-famous National Parks
Park | Country | Feature
Yellowstone | USA (mainly Wyoming; also Montana, Idaho) | First NP, 1872; Old Faithful geyser, hot springs, volcanic caldera, bison
Yosemite | USA (Sierra Nevada) | Granite cliffs, waterfalls, giant sequoias (no mangroves)
Grand Canyon | USA | Largest canyon landscape
Banff | Canada | Rocky Mountains; Canada's first NP (1885)
Galápagos | Ecuador | Endemic species; Darwin's study
Serengeti | Tanzania | Great Migration of wildebeest, zebra, gazelle
Kruger | South Africa | Savanna; Big Five – lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, buffalo (not zebra)
Masai Mara | Kenya | Continuation of the Serengeti
Ngorongoro | Tanzania | Crater wildlife
Okavango Delta | Botswana | Inland delta
Etosha | Namibia | Salt pan
Virunga | DR Congo | Mountain gorillas
Yellowstone is famous for geysers, but that is not why it was first – it was simply the first NP declared (1872).
# Andhra Pradesh Protected Areas
Notified forest 37,421.11 sq km (22.96%); PAs 8,139.88 sq km.
3 NPs: Sri Venkateswara (Tirupati/Chittoor; first, 1989), Papikonda (near Rajamahendravaram; largest), Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram; smallest); 13 WLS.
1 TR: Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam (Nallamala; largest by core/critical tiger habitat); 1 elephant reserve: Koundinya-Rayala; 1 BR: Seshachalam.
Rollapadu WLS – GIB; Coringa – mangroves; Nelapattu – birds.
Deer parks: Kandaleru (Rapur mandal, Nellore), Chittoor RF, Kotappakonda (Narsaraopeta, Palnadu).
Zoos: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (Visakhapatnam), Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park (Tirupati); Dolphin Conservation Society, Visakhapatnam – first ex-situ Biodiversity Park.
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP is in Hyderabad, Telangana – not AP.
# Number Game and Quick Revision
Item | Correct Fact
NPs / WLS | 109 / 573
Conservation / Community reserves | 127 / 75
Tiger / Elephant / Biosphere reserves | 58 / 33 / 18
UNESCO-listed BRs | 13
WPA assent | 9 Sep 1972
Corbett | 1936
Yellowstone / Banff | 1872 / 1885
Largest / smallest BR | Great Rann of Kutch 12,454 / Dibru-Saikhowa 765 sq km
## FIRST / LAST / SPECIAL FACTS
First NP: Corbett; first bird sanctuary: Vedanthangal; first wolf sanctuary: Mahuadanr.
First BR: Nilgiri (1986); latest UNESCO BR: Cold Desert (2025).
Only floating NP: Keibul Lamjao. First NP mascot: Bhoorsingh (Kanha).
# Appsc Previous Year Questions
Examination | Question Area
Group 1 Prelims 2024, Paper 2 | Biosphere Reserve → district location
APPSC 2025 | Corbett → Uttarakhand
APPSC 2024 | First bird sanctuary – Vedanthangal; Keoladeo → Rajasthan
APPSC 2023 | Balpakram → Meghalaya; Betla → Jharkhand; Pitti → Lakshadweep; Neora Valley → West Bengal
# High-probability Mcq Traps
1. Conservation reserve = government land; community reserve = private/community land.
2. Balpakram and Nokrek – Meghalaya (Garo Hills), not Manipur or Khasi Hills.
3. Hangul = Dachigam; Barasingha = Kanha; musk deer = Askot/Kedarnath.
4. Mouling – Arunachal, not Assam; Similipal – Odisha, not MP; Guindy – Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.
5. Corbett rivers Ramganga and Kosi, not Ganga; Kaziranga – Brahmaputra, Diphlu, not Manas.
6. Largest BR Great Rann of Kutch; smallest Dibru-Saikhowa; first Nilgiri.
7. Kruger Big Five excludes the zebra.
8. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP – Telangana.
9. Indravati WLS/NP – Chhattisgarh, not MP.
10. Western Ghats WHS – six states, 2012.

=== APPSC Prep notes ===

system.text:
You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Energy Resources - Coal, Petroleum, Gas, Hydel, Nuclear, Renewable; India and Ap

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Classification of Energy Sources
Class | Sources | Key point
Renewable (replenished naturally, short period) | Solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, tidal, wave, biomass, biogas | Basis of the energy transition
Non-renewable (finite) | Fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) + nuclear fuel (uranium, thorium) | Fossil fuels formed over millions of years; burning gives CO2
Uranium = non-renewable nuclear fuel, NOT a fossil fuel. Wood is not a fossil fuel. Natural gas is not renewable.
First source of fossil-fuel energy = the Sun (energy stored in buried organisms).
Petroleum: non-renewable, from ancient marine organisms; gives plastic toothbrushes and gasoline.
Petroleum products: petrol, diesel, kerosene, LPG, naphtha, bitumen, petrochemical feedstock. Anthracite is coal, not a petroleum product.
Commercial sources: power, coal, oil, gas, hydro-electricity, uranium. Biogas = non-commercial.
Non-conventional energy = renewable energy; biomass = renewable organic material.
APPSC 2025 keys: solar = not a fossil fuel; wind = renewable; solar + wind = energy-transition sources; thermal plants burn fossil fuels; solar plants use radiation, not coal.
Fossil fuels: ~75% of global GHGs, ~90% of CO2; subsidies $1.8 trillion (2024). Largest SO2 source: fossil-fuel power plants (73%).
First oil crisis: 1973 (OPEC raised oil price four times). Photovoltaic = solar to electricity; National Solar Mission under NAPCC.
Earth's resources include water, minerals, fish stocks, fossil fuels.
## Fuels and Composition
Fuel | Composition
Natural gas / CNG | Mainly methane (70-90%), ethane
LPG | Propane + butane
Biogas | Methane 50-75%, CO2 25-50%; anaerobic digestion; gives power + manure
Water gas | CO + H2
Producer gas | CO + H2 + N2
Coal gas | H2, methane, CO
Petrol / Kerosene / Diesel | C5-C10 / C10-C16 / C15-C18 (fractional distillation of crude)
Hydrogen | Electrolysis or steam reforming
Green hydrogen = RE-powered electrolysis; blue hydrogen = gas + CCS.
# India's Energy Data and Targets
Item | Fact
Installed capacity | ~552 GW (Aug 2026)
Non-fossil share | 51.93% (Dec 2025) - 50% target of 2030 reached ~5 years early
Solar / Wind / Bio-power | 164.59 GW (largest RE) / 58.14 GW / 11.75 GW
Hydro | ~48 GW (June 2025)
Coal | ~55% of primary energy; over 70% of electricity
Thermal (31 Dec 2025) | 48.07% of 513,729.69 MW - highest share
Nuclear (31 Dec 2025) | 8,780 MW = 1.71% of capacity; ~3% of generation
Global rank | 3rd in RE, 3rd in solar, 4th in wind
Targets: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; net zero 2070 (2050 for many developed countries); gas share 6.7% to 15% by 2030; battery storage ~47 GW by 2032.
Gujarat = 1st in gross installed capacity (Dec 2025) and RE (42.58 GW, 16.5%).
Geothermal potential ~10,600 MW (not installed); wind potential 695.5 GW at 120 m (1,163.9 GW at 150 m).
Peak demand 256 GW (Apr 2026); ~150 GW solar goes offline after sunset - night grid stress.
India 3rd in RE Country Attractiveness Index 2021.
# Coal
## Grades
Grade | Carbon | Occurrence
Anthracite | 80-95% (highest) | Only J&K, small
Bituminous | 40-80% | Most used; Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Chhattisgarh, MP
Lignite (brown coal) | 40-55% | High moisture; Neyveli (TN), Palana (Rajasthan), Gujarat, Lakhimpur, Karewa
Peat | <40% | First stage of wood turning to coal
## Gondwana vs Tertiary
Type | Age | Where
Gondwana | 250-300 mn yr | Damodar valley (largest), Mahanadi, Godavari, Son
Tertiary | 15-60 mn yr | North-East (Assam, Meghalaya); lignite: TN, Rajasthan, Gujarat
Jharkhand = largest coal reserves, no major lignite. Tamil Nadu = largest lignite (48.65% of output 2024-25; Gujarat 29.46%, Rajasthan 21.88%); India's lignite 47.36 bn t (1 Apr 2023).
Neyveli: first lignite-fired TPS in South-East Asia.
## Coalfields
Coalfield | State / fact
Raniganj | West Bengal (and Jharkhand); first mine 1774, Sitarampur, Damodar; maximum reserves (24,632.83 MT)
Jharia | Jharkhand (Dhanbad); main coking coal; underground fires; 19,430.06 MT
Bokaro, Giridih, Karanpura, Ramgarh | Jharkhand

Korba | Chhattisgarh
Singrauli, Sohagpur, Umaria | MP / Chhattisgarh
Singareni | Telangana, Godavari valley (SCCL)
Makum | Assam
Mawlong | East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya (not Arunachal)
Neyveli, Jayamkondam | Tamil Nadu (lignite)
## Mining, PSUs, Rank
Opencast = main method. Rat-hole mining (Meghalaya): narrow pits up to 400 ft, simple tools, small family groups (APPSC 2025 key: "mining by the family members"); banned by NGT 2014.
CIL = world's largest coal producer; SCCL = Telangana:Centre 51:49; NLC India = Neyveli lignite.
Coal Controller's Organisation (1916): coal statistics; statistical authority under Collection of Statistics Act 2008.
Revised SHAKTI (May 2025): coal through two windows.
World: China largest producer (51.78%) and consumer; India 2nd producer (11.11%) and consumer, 5th in reserves; reserves (end 2023): USA, Russia, China, Australia, India.
AP: coal mining was a main activity before colonial rule; after bifurcation AP lost its coal mines - higher transport cost.
# Petroleum and Natural Gas
## Oil History and Fields
First oil well: Makum, upper Assam, 26 March 1867 (118 ft); Digboi = first commercial find, production 1889; oldest oil town.
First petroleum detection: Margherita (Assam). Naharkatiya ~32 km SW of Digboi.

Barmer (Mangala, Bhagyam, Aishwariya) | Rajasthan
KG basin (KG-D6) | Andhra Pradesh
Rawa | AP; crude exported via single buoy mooring
Shale gas basins: Cambay (largest estimate), Assam-Arakan, Gondwana (Damodar), KG, Cauvery, Indo-Gangetic.
Exploration: ONGC and Oil India Ltd. India imports ~88% of its crude.
Oil trap order (bottom up): water → oil → gas, settled by density in an anticline under impermeable cap rock.
## Refineries
Capacity 258.1 MMTPA (June 2026); India = 4th largest refiner. Field-based (Digboi) vs market-based (Barauni, Mathura).

Hatia (Jharkhand) has no refinery. Assam has Digboi, Guwahati, Numaligarh, Bongaigaon.
## Reserves, SPR and Gas Grid
SPR (ISPRL): Padur, Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru (~5.33 MMT, ~9.5 days); Phase-II Chandikhol + Padur; Ankleshwar not selected.
PM Urja Ganga: Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra; national grid target over 32,000 km.

Gas: Russia largest reserves (not Qatar); USA top producer; Qatar major LNG exporter.
Alaska: oil state of USA, bought from Russia 1867. Donbass region = coal.
Hormuz closure (March 2026): India turned to coal and gas, LNG and LPG from other suppliers.
# Thermal Power Stations
Station | District, State
Vindhyachal | Singrauli, MP - largest (4,760 MW, NTPC)
Mundra | Kutch, Gujarat - 4,620 MW, second
Singrauli STPS / Rihand / Obra | Sonbhadra, UP (Obra: Russian help, 1967)

Vindhyachal is in Singrauli district (MP); Singrauli station is in Sonbhadra (UP).
Thermal industry = maximum water consumer; some plants use seawater, some are in water-stressed districts, some private.
Fly ash = by-product; Indian coal 30-45% ash, imported 10-15%. Coal plants run round the clock at 60-85% PLF.
Dadri (NTPC) – Gautam Buddh Nagar, UP.
# Hydel Power
Most potential in Himalayan basins (Brahmaputra, Indus, Ganga): snow-fed perennial flow, steep slopes - suit large dams and run-of-the-river. Peninsular rivers seasonal.
Arunachal Pradesh = highest hydel potential.
Pumped storage stores daytime solar power for night peaks; off-stream closed-loop PSPs no longer need CEA approval.
First hydropower station: Sidrapong, Darjeeling (1897); Shivasamudram (Kaveri, Karnataka) second oldest. NHPC set up 1975.

system.text:
You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

content.text:
STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Relevance of Science and Technology to Day-to-day Life

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Harmful Chemicals and Food Adulterants
Chemical | Found in / source
Rhodamine B | Textile dye illegally used to colour cotton candy; carcinogenic; sale banned in Tamil Nadu
Aristolochic acid | Aristolochia plants in some herbal medicines
BPA | Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings, thermal receipts
Triclosan | Antibacterial soaps, toothpaste, deodorants
Lead | Old paints, pipes, cosmetics, lead-chromate spices; not an MRI contrast agent
Phthalates | PVC plasticisers, toys, cosmetics
Food | Adulterant
Mustard oil | Argemone oil, causes epidemic dropsy
Turmeric | Metanil yellow, lead chromate
Milk / chilli | Water, urea, starch / brick powder, Sudan dyes
Mustard oil is NOT a lubricant: mineral oil = petroleum; vegetable fats = phytosterol; animal fats = cholesterol.
# Food Technology - Additives, Preservation, Fortification
## Additives vs Adulterants
Food additives = added intentionally to improve food (preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners, flavour enhancers). Adulteration = adding inferior/harmful substances; causes poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency.
Sweeteners: aspartame, stevia; fructose = natural sugar. MSG (Ajinomoto) = flavour enhancer, umami.
## Preservatives
Preservative | Used in
Sodium benzoate (E211) | Soft drinks, pickles, sauces (acidic foods)
Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate | Cheese, pickles; against yeasts, moulds
Sodium metabisulphite | Jams, sauces
SO2 | Dried fruits, winemaking
Propionates | Stored grains, cheese
Vinegar (acetic acid) | Pickles; made by fermenting sugarcane juice
Boric acid | Old, no longer used (toxic)
## Irradiation, Fortification, Cold Chain
Irradiation: ionising (gamma) radiation kills organisms without much nutrient loss; potato/onion shelf life 8 months without cold storage. DAE: 25 irradiators in PPP mode.
PM Kisan Sampada Yojana (MoFPI) Cold Chain scheme: 16 irradiation units approved, 9 operational (Aug 2025).
Fortification: iodised salt; rice with iron, folic acid, B12; oil/milk with A and D; FSSAI logo "+F".
Jul 2026: food-safety reforms - Food Safety on Wheels, blockchain batch tracing, "One Nation, One Regulator" ends dual BIS/AGMARK certification.
Kitchen: colas contain phosphoric acid and caffeine; lemon = citric acid; ant bite = formic acid (stronger than acetic acid).
Formic acid (methanoic acid) also acts as an antibacterial preservative; aspartame and stevia are sweeteners and fructose is a natural sugar, not preservatives.
# Nutrition and Vitamins
Vitamin | Name | Deficiency
A (fat) | Retinol | Night blindness, xerophthalmia
B1 | Thiamine | Beri-beri (polished rice)
B2 | Riboflavin | Cheilosis, glossitis
B3 | Niacin | Pellagra (not B5)
B5 | Pantothenic acid | Burning feet
B9 / B12 | Folic acid / Cobalamin (has cobalt) | Megaloblastic / pernicious anaemia
C | Ascorbic acid | Scurvy
D (fat) | Calciferol (D2 ergo-, D3 chole-) | Rickets, osteomalacia
E (fat) | Tocopherol | Sterility
K (fat) | Naphthoquinone | Slow clotting
Sources: vit C - amla (richest), chilli (vegetables), papaya; vit A - carrot, mango (fruits), Golden Rice (beta carotene); vit E - wheat germ oil; milk is poor in vit C and A. Vit C not stored; B12 and K made by gut bacteria; vit A stored in liver.
Scientists: Casimir Funk coined "vitamine"; James Lind - citrus cures scurvy; Hopkins - accessory food factors; McCollum and Davis - vit A (1913); Suzuki - rice bran extract.
Nutrients: carbohydrate = main energy; fat = 9.3 kcal/g; protein ~4 kcal/g. Highest protein grain soybean; groundnut rich (~25% protein); highest biological value egg; iodine seaweed; alpha-linolenic acid linseed; carbohydrate rice.
Proteins: casein (milk), gluten (wheat), keratin (hair, nails), collagen, fibroin (silk); oxytocin is NOT a protein. Kwashiorkor (oedema) and marasmus = protein deficiency. Nursing mother 65 g/day.
Amino acids: 20 (10 essential); not stored. Protein digestion starts in stomach (pepsin), then trypsin.
Pyridoxine = vitamin B6: amino-acid metabolism and antibody production; deficiency → anaemia, dermatitis.
Vitamin K sources: green leafy vegetables, also nuts, eggs and animal liver; needed for blood clotting.
Parboiling (soak + steam) raises rice's nutritive value: B vitamins move from bran into grain; polished raw rice → beri-beri.
Stomach HCl: from parietal (oxyntic) cells; pH ~1.5-3.5; activates pepsinogen → pepsin, kills microbes.
More vitamins: B7 = biotin (vitamin H); B-group vitamins (B1, B9 etc.) and vitamin C are water-soluble, while A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. McCollum, co-discoverer of vitamin A, also identified vitamin D (1922) as the anti-rickets factor in cod-liver oil.
# Human Body - Glands and Kidney
Gland | Hormone / fact
Pituitary (master) | GH, TSH, ACTH, ADH; oxytocin released here, made in hypothalamus
Pineal | Melatonin - biological clock
Thyroid (largest endocrine) | T3, T4 (iodine), calcitonin; deficiency: cretinism
Parathyroid | PTH - blood calcium
Adrenal (on kidney) | Adrenaline, cortisol
Pancreas | Endocrine + exocrine; insulin from Islets of Langerhans
Kidney / placenta | Erythropoietin / chorionic gonadotropin
Urea made in the liver, filtered by kidney; urine ~1.5 L/day, pH ~6.0; albumin in urine = kidney failure (Bright's disease). Normal BP 120/80 mmHg.
Dialysis when kidneys fail: haemodialysis (machine filter) vs peritoneal (peritoneum). Lithotripsy breaks stones with ultrasound.
Liver: largest gland (bile, glycogen, detox); regrows after partial removal → living-donor transplants.
Insulin (beta cells) lowers blood sugar, promotes glucose uptake and fat storage; glucagon (alpha) raises it. Type 1 diabetes = low insulin; type 2 = insulin resistance.
Blood groups: Landsteiner (1901); AB = universal recipient, O negative = universal donor.
Pacemaker: natural = SA node (right atrium); artificial pacemaker sends electric pulses to regulate heartbeat.
Gland locations: pituitary - at the base of the brain; thymus - behind the sternum, trains T cells; thyroid - front of the neck; adrenals - above the kidneys (adrenaline, cortisol, aldosterone); parathyroid - back (dorsal side) of the thyroid; pineal - in the brain (epithalamus), not on the kidney; testes (in the scrotum) - sperm and testosterone.
Blood cells: neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes (white blood cells) in human blood.
# Health Technologies - Imaging and Telemedicine
Method | Principle
X-ray (Rontgen) | Ionising radiation; not bent by fields
CT scan | X-rays + computer cross-sections
MRI | Magnetic field + radio waves on hydrogen nuclei; not ionising
Ultrasound | Sound >20 kHz echoes; safe for foetus
Audible 20 Hz-20 kHz; infrasound <20 Hz (earthquakes). Bats and SONAR use ultrasound.
Telemedicine: fibre backbone + satellite; eSanjeevani = national telemedicine. Chitra heart valve - SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram. Wearables give real-time data.
AP: AIIMS Mangalagiri - telemedicine, AI screening, epidemiology unit mapping outbreaks and NCDs.
Garbhini-GA2: India's first India-specific AI model for fetal age (2nd-3rd trimester); IIT Madras + THSTI Faridabad (GARBH-Ini).
ARTSENS: IIT Madras non-invasive device measuring arterial stiffness / vascular age; not for neurons.
Waves and uses: X-rays - medical imaging, security scanning; light waves - vision, optical fibres; radio waves - broadcasting; ultrasound - sonography, cleaning jewellery, industrial testing (finding cracks and flaws in metals), SONAR (underwater detection).
# Geospatial Technology in Public Health
Platform | Use
IHIP of IDSP | GIS real-time disease surveillance
Aarogya Setu | Contact tracing via Bluetooth + GPS
National One Health Mission | Zoonoses, AMR
Anna Chakra | PDS routes to 4.37 lakh shops; saves ~Rs 250 crore/yr
National One Health Mission: brings together the Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and Science and Technology ministries to tackle zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.
# Household Appliances and Chemicals
Appliance | Principle
Microwave oven | Magnetron; ~2.45 GHz rotates water molecules
Refrigerator | Vapour-compression; open door warms room
Induction cooktop | Electromagnetic induction, eddy currents
LED | Electroluminescence
RO purifier | Pressure against osmosis; desalination
Pressure cooker | Higher pressure raises boiling point (~120 C)
Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series
Washing machine | Centrifugation
Chemical | Fact
Baking soda | NaHCO3; CO2, antacid
Washing soda | Na2CO3
Teflon | PTFE non-stick
Hypo | Na2S2O3, photo fixer
Bleaching powder | Calcium oxychloride; disinfectant
Milk of magnesia | Mg(OH)2 antacid
Soap: alkaline, poor lather in hard water; detergent lathers well. Antiseptics on living tissue (H2O2, iodoform); disinfectants on objects (phenol).
Polymers: PVC - vinyl chloride; Teflon - tetrafluoroethene; neoprene - chloroprene; natural rubber - isoprene; Bakelite - phenol + formaldehyde; PHBV biodegradable.
Hard water: Ca/Mg salts form scum with soap; bicarbonates = temporary (boiling, Clark's lime); chlorides/sulphates = permanent (washing soda, ion exchange, Calgon).
Alloys: brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; German silver Cu-Zn-Ni; solder Sn-Pb; Dow metal = Mg + Al; boiler superheater tubes = Cr-Mo steel.
Metals: tungsten bulb filament (highest melting point); nichrome heater coil; aluminium most used in pure form (foil, cables), iron mostly as steel; sodium kept in kerosene.
Gold: 24 carat pure; 22 carat = 91.6% (916 hallmark, ~8.4% Cu/Ag); 18 carat = 75%; dissolves in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3).
Materials: PVC blood bags and dialysis tubes; glass wool = fine glass fibres (heat/sound insulation); flint (lead) glass lenses, prisms; Pyrex labware.
Others: CO2 extinguisher suits electrical fires; ruby = Al2O3 + chromium; Statue of Liberty green = copper patina; alkanes burn to CO2 + water + heat (⚠ APPSC key 2017 gave carbon).
Colloids: blood and milk are colloids; milk = emulsion of fat in water (butter = water in fat); ⚠ APPSC key (2002) gave water dispersed in fat.
Carbon forms and uses: diamond - jewellery, cutting, drilling and grinding tools, glass cutters; graphite - pencil 'lead', dry lubricant, electrodes, reactor moderator, Li-ion battery anodes; coke - fuel and reducing agent in iron extraction; carbon black (lampblack) - pigment in paints, inks, tyres; activated charcoal - adsorbs gases (gas masks), purification; fullerenes and carbon nanotubes - electronics, nanotechnology, drug delivery, lubricants, catalysts; graphene - electronics, composites, sensors, flexible devices.
More polymers: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 = glycine + amino caproic acid (biodegradable); PHBV = 3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid (biodegradable); nylon-6,6 = hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid; terylene = ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid; Buna-S = 1,3-butadiene + styrene; Buna-N = 1,3-butadiene + acrylonitrile.
Electromagnetic induction is used in generators, transformers, induction cooktops, wireless charging and the dynamic microphone (turns sound vibrations into electrical signals).
Refrigerator cycle: the refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside the refrigerator and releases it at the condenser outside.
Osmosis: water (solvent) moves through a semi-permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration (plant roots absorb water this way); in reverse osmosis pressure is applied on the concentrated side, leaving salts and bacteria behind (desalination, water purification).
Bleaching powder releases chlorine, so it is used for water purification and bleaching. Disinfectants (phenol, bleaching powder) are toxic to living tissue, so they are used only on objects; antiseptics (boric acid, iodoform, H2O2) are safe on living tissue.
Soap vs detergent: soap is biodegradable but its alkaline solution harms silk and wool; detergents suit delicate clothes; many older detergents had branched chains that bacteria could not break down, so they were non-biodegradable and caused foam in rivers.
# Smart Materials and Sensors
Hydrogels: up to 99% water; contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery.
Accelerometer (MEMS): triggers airbags, laptop free-fall detection, step counting. MEMS also in gyroscopes, microphones.
Flexible batteries power wearables.
# Transport Technologies
Technology | Fact
FASTag | Passive RFID
Metro card | Passive NFC, 13.56 MHz, ~4 cm
GPS | India's own: NavIC
V2X | C-V2X = 4G/5G; DSRC = Wi-Fi
Hydrogen fuel cell | Emits only water
EVs: PM E-DRIVE scheme (Ministry of Heavy Industries) extended to 31 March 2028.
Black box (flight data recorder + cockpit voice recorder): fitted in the tail to survive crashes ⚠ APPSC key (2004) gave cockpit.

## Everyday Physics and Chemistry Basics
Units: henry = inductance; farad = capacitance; pascal = pressure; decibel = sound level; angstrom = 10^-10 m; light year = distance; picosecond = 10^-12 s.
Instruments: lactometer = milk purity (specific gravity); hygrometer = humidity; barometer = pressure; anemometer = wind speed; atomic (caesium) clock = most exact time.
Optics: silvery crack in glass, diamond sparkle = total internal reflection; rainbow = refraction + dispersion + TIR; sky black in space (no scattering); convex mirror magnification <1.
Radiation: infrared heat therapy for muscular pain; X-rays strongly darken photographic plates; fan under AC lamp seems to reverse (stroboscopic effect).
Mechanics: mass measures inertia; friction opposes motion; doubling momentum makes KE x4 (+300%); no external force = centre-of-mass velocity constant; egg floats in denser salt water.
Electricity: transformer works only on AC; bird on a live wire is safe (no potential difference); unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole.
Heat: tea cools fastest in a metal cup (good conductor); free expansion = into vacuum, no work, ideal-gas temperature unchanged.
Matter: plasma (ionised gas) = 4th state, BEC = 5th; liquid crystals lie between solid and liquid, used in LCD.
Air: inhaled ~21% O2, 78% N2, 0.04% CO2; exhaled ~16% O2, 4% CO2.
Chemistry basics: OIL RIG (oxidation = electron loss); hydrogen = 'inflammable air' (Cavendish 1766), atomic number 1; silicon = 2nd most abundant crustal element after oxygen.
Molecules: chiral = Greek 'hand'; alkaloids contain nitrogen; excess Li makes LiCl pink (F-centres); energy-absorbing reactions = endergonic, energy-releasing = exergonic.
Physics principles: equivalence principle - basis of general relativity, used in GPS time corrections; Doppler principle - red shift of receding galaxies, Doppler ultrasound; Huygens' principle - every point on a wavefront is a source, explains wave propagation, reflection and refraction; Pascal's - hydraulic lift, syringe; Archimedes' - buoyancy; Bernoulli's - wing lift; conservation of momentum - gun recoil, rocket propulsion; conservation of angular momentum - an ice-skater spins faster on pulling in the arms, planetary orbits.
Electrical units: resistance - ohm; resistivity - ohm-metre (ρ = RA/l); conductance (G = 1/R) - siemens, older unit mho; conductivity (1/ρ) - siemens per metre (S/m); elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (1 C = charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons); conventional current flows from positive to negative, opposite to electron flow.
Convex lens (converging): object within F gives a virtual, erect, magnified image (magnifying glass); it forms real images in a camera, compound microscope and telescope; a burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point.
Myopia (short-sightedness): the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina; corrected by a concave lens of negative power.

## 1. Electrical quantities and units
Quantity | SI unit | Facts
Electric charge | Coulomb (C) — also esu and emu | Elementary charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; one coulomb = the charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons
Electric current | Ampere (A) — 1 A = 1 C/s (one coulomb per second) | Small currents: milliamperes (mA), microamperes (μA); conventional direction positive → negative; electron flow negative → positive

Conductivity | Siemens per metre (S/m) | The reciprocal of resistivity — σ = 1/ρ

Power | Watt (W) — commercial: kilowatt (kW), megawatt (MW) | One kilowatt = 1000 watts; one horsepower = 746 watts
## 2. Electric fuse
Principle: The heating effect of current
Material: A low-melting-point alloy — tin-lead
Melts when current exceeds its rated value — breaks the circuit; melts immediately during a short circuit
Placed in series with the device or circuit — overcurrent protection prevents damage due to excess current
Household wiring: A main fuse and individual circuit fuses; some appliances have built-in fuses
## 1. Uses of electromagnetic induction
Generators — power generation; transformers — voltage conversion
Induction cooktops — heating
Wireless charging — mobile phones and electric vehicles
Magnetic brakes in trains
Dynamic microphones; induction motors (industrial)
EMI sensors; metal detectors
## 2. Osmosis and reverse osmosis
Osmosis: Movement of solvent (water) through a semipermeable membrane — from low to high solute concentration; plant roots absorb water by osmosis
Reverse osmosis: External pressure on the concentrated side — solvent moves from high to low concentration
Uses: Desalination of seawater; purification of water — removes ions and bacteria

system.text:
You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

content.text:
STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Relevance of Science and Technology to Day-to-day Life

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Harmful Chemicals and Food Adulterants
Chemical | Found in / source
Rhodamine B | Textile dye illegally used to colour cotton candy; carcinogenic; sale banned in Tamil Nadu
Aristolochic acid | Aristolochia plants in some herbal medicines
BPA | Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings, thermal receipts
Triclosan | Antibacterial soaps, toothpaste, deodorants
Lead | Old paints, pipes, cosmetics, lead-chromate spices; not an MRI contrast agent
Phthalates | PVC plasticisers, toys, cosmetics
Food | Adulterant
Mustard oil | Argemone oil, causes epidemic dropsy
Turmeric | Metanil yellow, lead chromate
Milk / chilli | Water, urea, starch / brick powder, Sudan dyes
Mustard oil is NOT a lubricant: mineral oil = petroleum; vegetable fats = phytosterol; animal fats = cholesterol.
# Food Technology - Additives, Preservation, Fortification
## Additives vs Adulterants
Food additives = added intentionally to improve food (preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners, flavour enhancers). Adulteration = adding inferior/harmful substances; causes poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency.
Sweeteners: aspartame, stevia; fructose = natural sugar. MSG (Ajinomoto) = flavour enhancer, umami.
## Preservatives
Preservative | Used in
Sodium benzoate (E211) | Soft drinks, pickles, sauces (acidic foods)
Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate | Cheese, pickles; against yeasts, moulds
Sodium metabisulphite | Jams, sauces
SO2 | Dried fruits, winemaking
Propionates | Stored grains, cheese
Vinegar (acetic acid) | Pickles; made by fermenting sugarcane juice
Boric acid | Old, no longer used (toxic)
## Irradiation, Fortification, Cold Chain
Irradiation: ionising (gamma) radiation kills organisms without much nutrient loss; potato/onion shelf life 8 months without cold storage. DAE: 25 irradiators in PPP mode.
PM Kisan Sampada Yojana (MoFPI) Cold Chain scheme: 16 irradiation units approved, 9 operational (Aug 2025).
Fortification: iodised salt; rice with iron, folic acid, B12; oil/milk with A and D; FSSAI logo "+F".
Jul 2026: food-safety reforms - Food Safety on Wheels, blockchain batch tracing, "One Nation, One Regulator" ends dual BIS/AGMARK certification.
Kitchen: colas contain phosphoric acid and caffeine; lemon = citric acid; ant bite = formic acid (stronger than acetic acid).
Formic acid (methanoic acid) also acts as an antibacterial preservative; aspartame and stevia are sweeteners and fructose is a natural sugar, not preservatives.
# Nutrition and Vitamins
Vitamin | Name | Deficiency
A (fat) | Retinol | Night blindness, xerophthalmia
B1 | Thiamine | Beri-beri (polished rice)
B2 | Riboflavin | Cheilosis, glossitis
B3 | Niacin | Pellagra (not B5)
B5 | Pantothenic acid | Burning feet
B9 / B12 | Folic acid / Cobalamin (has cobalt) | Megaloblastic / pernicious anaemia
C | Ascorbic acid | Scurvy
D (fat) | Calciferol (D2 ergo-, D3 chole-) | Rickets, osteomalacia
E (fat) | Tocopherol | Sterility
K (fat) | Naphthoquinone | Slow clotting
Sources: vit C - amla (richest), chilli (vegetables), papaya; vit A - carrot, mango (fruits), Golden Rice (beta carotene); vit E - wheat germ oil; milk is poor in vit C and A. Vit C not stored; B12 and K made by gut bacteria; vit A stored in liver.
Scientists: Casimir Funk coined "vitamine"; James Lind - citrus cures scurvy; Hopkins - accessory food factors; McCollum and Davis - vit A (1913); Suzuki - rice bran extract.
Nutrients: carbohydrate = main energy; fat = 9.3 kcal/g; protein ~4 kcal/g. Highest protein grain soybean; groundnut rich (~25% protein); highest biological value egg; iodine seaweed; alpha-linolenic acid linseed; carbohydrate rice.
Proteins: casein (milk), gluten (wheat), keratin (hair, nails), collagen, fibroin (silk); oxytocin is NOT a protein. Kwashiorkor (oedema) and marasmus = protein deficiency. Nursing mother 65 g/day.
Amino acids: 20 (10 essential); not stored. Protein digestion starts in stomach (pepsin), then trypsin.
Pyridoxine = vitamin B6: amino-acid metabolism and antibody production; deficiency → anaemia, dermatitis.
Vitamin K sources: green leafy vegetables, also nuts, eggs and animal liver; needed for blood clotting.
Parboiling (soak + steam) raises rice's nutritive value: B vitamins move from bran into grain; polished raw rice → beri-beri.
Stomach HCl: from parietal (oxyntic) cells; pH ~1.5-3.5; activates pepsinogen → pepsin, kills microbes.
More vitamins: B7 = biotin (vitamin H); B-group vitamins (B1, B9 etc.) and vitamin C are water-soluble, while A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. McCollum, co-discoverer of vitamin A, also identified vitamin D (1922) as the anti-rickets factor in cod-liver oil.
# Human Body - Glands and Kidney
Gland | Hormone / fact
Pituitary (master) | GH, TSH, ACTH, ADH; oxytocin released here, made in hypothalamus
Pineal | Melatonin - biological clock
Thyroid (largest endocrine) | T3, T4 (iodine), calcitonin; deficiency: cretinism
Parathyroid | PTH - blood calcium
Adrenal (on kidney) | Adrenaline, cortisol
Pancreas | Endocrine + exocrine; insulin from Islets of Langerhans
Kidney / placenta | Erythropoietin / chorionic gonadotropin
Urea made in the liver, filtered by kidney; urine ~1.5 L/day, pH ~6.0; albumin in urine = kidney failure (Bright's disease). Normal BP 120/80 mmHg.
Dialysis when kidneys fail: haemodialysis (machine filter) vs peritoneal (peritoneum). Lithotripsy breaks stones with ultrasound.
Liver: largest gland (bile, glycogen, detox); regrows after partial removal → living-donor transplants.
Insulin (beta cells) lowers blood sugar, promotes glucose uptake and fat storage; glucagon (alpha) raises it. Type 1 diabetes = low insulin; type 2 = insulin resistance.
Blood groups: Landsteiner (1901); AB = universal recipient, O negative = universal donor.
Pacemaker: natural = SA node (right atrium); artificial pacemaker sends electric pulses to regulate heartbeat.
Gland locations: pituitary - at the base of the brain; thymus - behind the sternum, trains T cells; thyroid - front of the neck; adrenals - above the kidneys (adrenaline, cortisol, aldosterone); parathyroid - back (dorsal side) of the thyroid; pineal - in the brain (epithalamus), not on the kidney; testes (in the scrotum) - sperm and testosterone.
Blood cells: neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes (white blood cells) in human blood.
# Health Technologies - Imaging and Telemedicine
Method | Principle
X-ray (Rontgen) | Ionising radiation; not bent by fields
CT scan | X-rays + computer cross-sections
MRI | Magnetic field + radio waves on hydrogen nuclei; not ionising
Ultrasound | Sound >20 kHz echoes; safe for foetus
Audible 20 Hz-20 kHz; infrasound <20 Hz (earthquakes). Bats and SONAR use ultrasound.
Telemedicine: fibre backbone + satellite; eSanjeevani = national telemedicine. Chitra heart valve - SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram. Wearables give real-time data.
AP: AIIMS Mangalagiri - telemedicine, AI screening, epidemiology unit mapping outbreaks and NCDs.
Garbhini-GA2: India's first India-specific AI model for fetal age (2nd-3rd trimester); IIT Madras + THSTI Faridabad (GARBH-Ini).
ARTSENS: IIT Madras non-invasive device measuring arterial stiffness / vascular age; not for neurons.
Waves and uses: X-rays - medical imaging, security scanning; light waves - vision, optical fibres; radio waves - broadcasting; ultrasound - sonography, cleaning jewellery, industrial testing (finding cracks and flaws in metals), SONAR (underwater detection).
# Geospatial Technology in Public Health
Platform | Use
IHIP of IDSP | GIS real-time disease surveillance
Aarogya Setu | Contact tracing via Bluetooth + GPS
National One Health Mission | Zoonoses, AMR
Anna Chakra | PDS routes to 4.37 lakh shops; saves ~Rs 250 crore/yr
National One Health Mission: brings together the Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and Science and Technology ministries to tackle zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.
# Household Appliances and Chemicals
Appliance | Principle
Microwave oven | Magnetron; ~2.45 GHz rotates water molecules
Refrigerator | Vapour-compression; open door warms room
Induction cooktop | Electromagnetic induction, eddy currents
LED | Electroluminescence
RO purifier | Pressure against osmosis; desalination
Pressure cooker | Higher pressure raises boiling point (~120 C)
Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series
Washing machine | Centrifugation
Chemical | Fact
Baking soda | NaHCO3; CO2, antacid
Washing soda | Na2CO3
Teflon | PTFE non-stick
Hypo | Na2S2O3, photo fixer
Bleaching powder | Calcium oxychloride; disinfectant
Milk of magnesia | Mg(OH)2 antacid
Soap: alkaline, poor lather in hard water; detergent lathers well. Antiseptics on living tissue (H2O2, iodoform); disinfectants on objects (phenol).
Polymers: PVC - vinyl chloride; Teflon - tetrafluoroethene; neoprene - chloroprene; natural rubber - isoprene; Bakelite - phenol + formaldehyde; PHBV biodegradable.
Hard water: Ca/Mg salts form scum with soap; bicarbonates = temporary (boiling, Clark's lime); chlorides/sulphates = permanent (washing soda, ion exchange, Calgon).
Alloys: brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; German silver Cu-Zn-Ni; solder Sn-Pb; Dow metal = Mg + Al; boiler superheater tubes = Cr-Mo steel.
Metals: tungsten bulb filament (highest melting point); nichrome heater coil; aluminium most used in pure form (foil, cables), iron mostly as steel; sodium kept in kerosene.
Gold: 24 carat pure; 22 carat = 91.6% (916 hallmark, ~8.4% Cu/Ag); 18 carat = 75%; dissolves in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3).
Materials: PVC blood bags and dialysis tubes; glass wool = fine glass fibres (heat/sound insulation); flint (lead) glass lenses, prisms; Pyrex labware.
Others: CO2 extinguisher suits electrical fires; ruby = Al2O3 + chromium; Statue of Liberty green = copper patina; alkanes burn to CO2 + water + heat (⚠ APPSC key 2017 gave carbon).
Colloids: blood and milk are colloids; milk = emulsion of fat in water (butter = water in fat); ⚠ APPSC key (2002) gave water dispersed in fat.
Carbon forms and uses: diamond - jewellery, cutting, drilling and grinding tools, glass cutters; graphite - pencil 'lead', dry lubricant, electrodes, reactor moderator, Li-ion battery anodes; coke - fuel and reducing agent in iron extraction; carbon black (lampblack) - pigment in paints, inks, tyres; activated charcoal - adsorbs gases (gas masks), purification; fullerenes and carbon nanotubes - electronics, nanotechnology, drug delivery, lubricants, catalysts; graphene - electronics, composites, sensors, flexible devices.
More polymers: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 = glycine + amino caproic acid (biodegradable); PHBV = 3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid (biodegradable); nylon-6,6 = hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid; terylene = ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid; Buna-S = 1,3-butadiene + styrene; Buna-N = 1,3-butadiene + acrylonitrile.
Electromagnetic induction is used in generators, transformers, induction cooktops, wireless charging and the dynamic microphone (turns sound vibrations into electrical signals).
Refrigerator cycle: the refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside the refrigerator and releases it at the condenser outside.
Osmosis: water (solvent) moves through a semi-permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration (plant roots absorb water this way); in reverse osmosis pressure is applied on the concentrated side, leaving salts and bacteria behind (desalination, water purification).
Bleaching powder releases chlorine, so it is used for water purification and bleaching. Disinfectants (phenol, bleaching powder) are toxic to living tissue, so they are used only on objects; antiseptics (boric acid, iodoform, H2O2) are safe on living tissue.
Soap vs detergent: soap is biodegradable but its alkaline solution harms silk and wool; detergents suit delicate clothes; many older detergents had branched chains that bacteria could not break down, so they were non-biodegradable and caused foam in rivers.
# Smart Materials and Sensors
Hydrogels: up to 99% water; contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery.
Accelerometer (MEMS): triggers airbags, laptop free-fall detection, step counting. MEMS also in gyroscopes, microphones.
Flexible batteries power wearables.
# Transport Technologies
Technology | Fact
FASTag | Passive RFID
Metro card | Passive NFC, 13.56 MHz, ~4 cm
GPS | India's own: NavIC
V2X | C-V2X = 4G/5G; DSRC = Wi-Fi
Hydrogen fuel cell | Emits only water
EVs: PM E-DRIVE scheme (Ministry of Heavy Industries) extended to 31 March 2028.
Black box (flight data recorder + cockpit voice recorder): fitted in the tail to survive crashes ⚠ APPSC key (2004) gave cockpit.
# Positive vs Negative Impacts
Positive | Negative
Communication, flexible work | Decreased privacy
Health tracking | Screen time, eye strain
Digital payments | Cyber fraud, digital divide
Aug 2026: Supreme Court sought Centre's reply on a plea on "high-risk" AI (biometric surveillance, risk-scoring in welfare delivery).
# Number Game and Quick Revision
Item | Fact
Food irradiators (DAE) | 25
Microwave frequency | 2.45 GHz
Ultrasound | >20 kHz
Normal BP | 120/80 mmHg
1 horsepower | 746 W
Lens power | Dioptre = 1/f (m)
## FIRST / LAST / SPECIAL FACTS
Concave lens corrects myopia; convex corrects hypermetropia; car headlight concave mirror, rear-view convex.
Boiling point falls with altitude; salt raises it. Pascal's law - hydraulic brakes; momentum - rockets.
## Everyday Physics and Chemistry Basics
Units: henry = inductance; farad = capacitance; pascal = pressure; decibel = sound level; angstrom = 10^-10 m; light year = distance; picosecond = 10^-12 s.
Instruments: lactometer = milk purity (specific gravity); hygrometer = humidity; barometer = pressure; anemometer = wind speed; atomic (caesium) clock = most exact time.
Optics: silvery crack in glass, diamond sparkle = total internal reflection; rainbow = refraction + dispersion + TIR; sky black in space (no scattering); convex mirror magnification <1.
Radiation: infrared heat therapy for muscular pain; X-rays strongly darken photographic plates; fan under AC lamp seems to reverse (stroboscopic effect).
Mechanics: mass measures inertia; friction opposes motion; doubling momentum makes KE x4 (+300%); no external force = centre-of-mass velocity constant; egg floats in denser salt water.
Electricity: transformer works only on AC; bird on a live wire is safe (no potential difference); unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole.
Heat: tea cools fastest in a metal cup (good conductor); free expansion = into vacuum, no work, ideal-gas temperature unchanged.
Matter: plasma (ionised gas) = 4th state, BEC = 5th; liquid crystals lie between solid and liquid, used in LCD.
Air: inhaled ~21% O2, 78% N2, 0.04% CO2; exhaled ~16% O2, 4% CO2.
Chemistry basics: OIL RIG (oxidation = electron loss); hydrogen = 'inflammable air' (Cavendish 1766), atomic number 1; silicon = 2nd most abundant crustal element after oxygen.
Molecules: chiral = Greek 'hand'; alkaloids contain nitrogen; excess Li makes LiCl pink (F-centres); energy-absorbing reactions = endergonic, energy-releasing = exergonic.
Physics principles: equivalence principle - basis of general relativity, used in GPS time corrections; Doppler principle - red shift of receding galaxies, Doppler ultrasound; Huygens' principle - every point on a wavefront is a source, explains wave propagation, reflection and refraction; Pascal's - hydraulic lift, syringe; Archimedes' - buoyancy; Bernoulli's - wing lift; conservation of momentum - gun recoil, rocket propulsion; conservation of angular momentum - an ice-skater spins faster on pulling in the arms, planetary orbits.
Electrical units: resistance - ohm; resistivity - ohm-metre (ρ = RA/l); conductance (G = 1/R) - siemens, older unit mho; conductivity (1/ρ) - siemens per metre (S/m); elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (1 C = charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons); conventional current flows from positive to negative, opposite to electron flow.
Convex lens (converging): object within F gives a virtual, erect, magnified image (magnifying glass); it forms real images in a camera, compound microscope and telescope; a burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point.
Myopia (short-sightedness): the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina; corrected by a concave lens of negative power.
# Appsc Previous Year Questions
Examination | Question Area
Group 1 Prelims 2024, Paper 2 | Rhodamine B - cotton candy; food additives
APPSC GS 2022 | Ultrasound for foetus (A and R); decreased privacy not a positive impact
APPSC GS 2019 | Dialysis when kidneys fail; food additives added intentionally
# High-probability Mcq Traps
1. Urea is made in the liver, not the kidney.
2. Pellagra = B3, not B5 or C; beri-beri = B1.
3. MRI uses radio waves, no ionising radiation; CT uses X-rays.
4. Additives are intentional; adulterants are harmful.
5. FASTag = RFID; metro card = NFC.
6. C-V2X = 4G/5G, DSRC = Wi-Fi.
7. Bleaching powder is a disinfectant; boric acid, iodoform, H2O2 are antiseptics.
8. Decreased privacy is a negative impact.
9. Fuse is in series; low melting point, high resistivity; ⚠ APPSC key (2012) gave low resistivity.

=== APPSC Prep notes ===
# Food and health terms — definitions and types
Term | Meaning
Dialysis | recommended when the kidneys fail (APPSC-GS 2019); removes wastes and excess water from blood
haemodialysis | machine filter
peritoneal dialysis | peritoneum as membrane
Food additives | chemicals added intentionally during production, processing or storage to improve the qualities of food (APPSC-GS 2019)
Adulteration | intentionally adding inferior/harmful substances
Irradiation | ionising radiation destroys harmful organisms without altering nutrition
Fortification | adding micronutrients
Additive types: preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners, flavour enhancers (MSG)
Adulteration effects: acute poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency
⚠ Additives = added intentionally to improve food; adulterants = inferior/harmful substances

Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:

- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED).
