content.text:
STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Relevance of Science and Technology to Day-to-day Life

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Harmful Chemicals and Food Adulterants
Chemical | Found in / source
Rhodamine B | Textile dye illegally used to colour cotton candy; carcinogenic; sale banned in Tamil Nadu
Aristolochic acid | Aristolochia plants in some herbal medicines
BPA | Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings, thermal receipts
Triclosan | Antibacterial soaps, toothpaste, deodorants
Lead | Old paints, pipes, cosmetics, lead-chromate spices; not an MRI contrast agent
Phthalates | PVC plasticisers, toys, cosmetics
Food | Adulterant
Mustard oil | Argemone oil, causes epidemic dropsy
Turmeric | Metanil yellow, lead chromate
Milk / chilli | Water, urea, starch / brick powder, Sudan dyes
Mustard oil is NOT a lubricant: mineral oil = petroleum; vegetable fats = phytosterol; animal fats = cholesterol.
# Food Technology - Additives, Preservation, Fortification
## Additives vs Adulterants
Food additives = added intentionally to improve food (preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners, flavour enhancers). Adulteration = adding inferior/harmful substances; causes poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency.
Sweeteners: aspartame, stevia; fructose = natural sugar. MSG (Ajinomoto) = flavour enhancer, umami.
## Preservatives
Preservative | Used in
Sodium benzoate (E211) | Soft drinks, pickles, sauces (acidic foods)
Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate | Cheese, pickles; against yeasts, moulds
Sodium metabisulphite | Jams, sauces
SO2 | Dried fruits, winemaking
Propionates | Stored grains, cheese
Vinegar (acetic acid) | Pickles; made by fermenting sugarcane juice
Boric acid | Old, no longer used (toxic)
## Irradiation, Fortification, Cold Chain
Irradiation: ionising (gamma) radiation kills organisms without much nutrient loss; potato/onion shelf life 8 months without cold storage. DAE: 25 irradiators in PPP mode.
PM Kisan Sampada Yojana (MoFPI) Cold Chain scheme: 16 irradiation units approved, 9 operational (Aug 2025).
Fortification: iodised salt; rice with iron, folic acid, B12; oil/milk with A and D; FSSAI logo "+F".
Jul 2026: food-safety reforms - Food Safety on Wheels, blockchain batch tracing, "One Nation, One Regulator" ends dual BIS/AGMARK certification.
Kitchen: colas contain phosphoric acid and caffeine; lemon = citric acid; ant bite = formic acid (stronger than acetic acid).
Formic acid (methanoic acid) also acts as an antibacterial preservative; aspartame and stevia are sweeteners and fructose is a natural sugar, not preservatives.
# Nutrition and Vitamins
Vitamin | Name | Deficiency
A (fat) | Retinol | Night blindness, xerophthalmia
B1 | Thiamine | Beri-beri (polished rice)
B2 | Riboflavin | Cheilosis, glossitis
B3 | Niacin | Pellagra (not B5)
B5 | Pantothenic acid | Burning feet
B9 / B12 | Folic acid / Cobalamin (has cobalt) | Megaloblastic / pernicious anaemia
C | Ascorbic acid | Scurvy
D (fat) | Calciferol (D2 ergo-, D3 chole-) | Rickets, osteomalacia
E (fat) | Tocopherol | Sterility
K (fat) | Naphthoquinone | Slow clotting
Sources: vit C - amla (richest), chilli (vegetables), papaya; vit A - carrot, mango (fruits), Golden Rice (beta carotene); vit E - wheat germ oil; milk is poor in vit C and A. Vit C not stored; B12 and K made by gut bacteria; vit A stored in liver.
Scientists: Casimir Funk coined "vitamine"; James Lind - citrus cures scurvy; Hopkins - accessory food factors; McCollum and Davis - vit A (1913); Suzuki - rice bran extract.
Nutrients: carbohydrate = main energy; fat = 9.3 kcal/g; protein ~4 kcal/g. Highest protein grain soybean; groundnut rich (~25% protein); highest biological value egg; iodine seaweed; alpha-linolenic acid linseed; carbohydrate rice.
Proteins: casein (milk), gluten (wheat), keratin (hair, nails), collagen, fibroin (silk); oxytocin is NOT a protein. Kwashiorkor (oedema) and marasmus = protein deficiency. Nursing mother 65 g/day.
Amino acids: 20 (10 essential); not stored. Protein digestion starts in stomach (pepsin), then trypsin.
Pyridoxine = vitamin B6: amino-acid metabolism and antibody production; deficiency → anaemia, dermatitis.
Vitamin K sources: green leafy vegetables, also nuts, eggs and animal liver; needed for blood clotting.
Parboiling (soak + steam) raises rice's nutritive value: B vitamins move from bran into grain; polished raw rice → beri-beri.
Stomach HCl: from parietal (oxyntic) cells; pH ~1.5-3.5; activates pepsinogen → pepsin, kills microbes.
More vitamins: B7 = biotin (vitamin H); B-group vitamins (B1, B9 etc.) and vitamin C are water-soluble, while A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. McCollum, co-discoverer of vitamin A, also identified vitamin D (1922) as the anti-rickets factor in cod-liver oil.
# Human Body - Glands and Kidney
Gland | Hormone / fact
Pituitary (master) | GH, TSH, ACTH, ADH; oxytocin released here, made in hypothalamus
Pineal | Melatonin - biological clock
Thyroid (largest endocrine) | T3, T4 (iodine), calcitonin; deficiency: cretinism
Parathyroid | PTH - blood calcium
Adrenal (on kidney) | Adrenaline, cortisol
Pancreas | Endocrine + exocrine; insulin from Islets of Langerhans
Kidney / placenta | Erythropoietin / chorionic gonadotropin
Urea made in the liver, filtered by kidney; urine ~1.5 L/day, pH ~6.0; albumin in urine = kidney failure (Bright's disease). Normal BP 120/80 mmHg.
Dialysis when kidneys fail: haemodialysis (machine filter) vs peritoneal (peritoneum). Lithotripsy breaks stones with ultrasound.
Liver: largest gland (bile, glycogen, detox); regrows after partial removal → living-donor transplants.
Insulin (beta cells) lowers blood sugar, promotes glucose uptake and fat storage; glucagon (alpha) raises it. Type 1 diabetes = low insulin; type 2 = insulin resistance.
Blood groups: Landsteiner (1901); AB = universal recipient, O negative = universal donor.
Pacemaker: natural = SA node (right atrium); artificial pacemaker sends electric pulses to regulate heartbeat.
Gland locations: pituitary - at the base of the brain; thymus - behind the sternum, trains T cells; thyroid - front of the neck; adrenals - above the kidneys (adrenaline, cortisol, aldosterone); parathyroid - back (dorsal side) of the thyroid; pineal - in the brain (epithalamus), not on the kidney; testes (in the scrotum) - sperm and testosterone.
Blood cells: neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes (white blood cells) in human blood.
# Health Technologies - Imaging and Telemedicine
Method | Principle
X-ray (Rontgen) | Ionising radiation; not bent by fields
CT scan | X-rays + computer cross-sections
MRI | Magnetic field + radio waves on hydrogen nuclei; not ionising
Ultrasound | Sound >20 kHz echoes; safe for foetus
Audible 20 Hz-20 kHz; infrasound <20 Hz (earthquakes). Bats and SONAR use ultrasound.
Telemedicine: fibre backbone + satellite; eSanjeevani = national telemedicine. Chitra heart valve - SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram. Wearables give real-time data.
AP: AIIMS Mangalagiri - telemedicine, AI screening, epidemiology unit mapping outbreaks and NCDs.
Garbhini-GA2: India's first India-specific AI model for fetal age (2nd-3rd trimester); IIT Madras + THSTI Faridabad (GARBH-Ini).
ARTSENS: IIT Madras non-invasive device measuring arterial stiffness / vascular age; not for neurons.
Waves and uses: X-rays - medical imaging, security scanning; light waves - vision, optical fibres; radio waves - broadcasting; ultrasound - sonography, cleaning jewellery, industrial testing (finding cracks and flaws in metals), SONAR (underwater detection).
# Geospatial Technology in Public Health
Platform | Use
IHIP of IDSP | GIS real-time disease surveillance
Aarogya Setu | Contact tracing via Bluetooth + GPS
National One Health Mission | Zoonoses, AMR
Anna Chakra | PDS routes to 4.37 lakh shops; saves ~Rs 250 crore/yr
National One Health Mission: brings together the Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and Science and Technology ministries to tackle zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.
# Household Appliances and Chemicals
Appliance | Principle
Microwave oven | Magnetron; ~2.45 GHz rotates water molecules
Refrigerator | Vapour-compression; open door warms room
Induction cooktop | Electromagnetic induction, eddy currents
LED | Electroluminescence
RO purifier | Pressure against osmosis; desalination
Pressure cooker | Higher pressure raises boiling point (~120 C)
Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series
Washing machine | Centrifugation
Chemical | Fact
Baking soda | NaHCO3; CO2, antacid
Washing soda | Na2CO3
Teflon | PTFE non-stick
Hypo | Na2S2O3, photo fixer
Bleaching powder | Calcium oxychloride; disinfectant
Milk of magnesia | Mg(OH)2 antacid
Soap: alkaline, poor lather in hard water; detergent lathers well. Antiseptics on living tissue (H2O2, iodoform); disinfectants on objects (phenol).
Polymers: PVC - vinyl chloride; Teflon - tetrafluoroethene; neoprene - chloroprene; natural rubber - isoprene; Bakelite - phenol + formaldehyde; PHBV biodegradable.
Hard water: Ca/Mg salts form scum with soap; bicarbonates = temporary (boiling, Clark's lime); chlorides/sulphates = permanent (washing soda, ion exchange, Calgon).
Alloys: brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; German silver Cu-Zn-Ni; solder Sn-Pb; Dow metal = Mg + Al; boiler superheater tubes = Cr-Mo steel.
Metals: tungsten bulb filament (highest melting point); nichrome heater coil; aluminium most used in pure form (foil, cables), iron mostly as steel; sodium kept in kerosene.
Gold: 24 carat pure; 22 carat = 91.6% (916 hallmark, ~8.4% Cu/Ag); 18 carat = 75%; dissolves in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3).
Materials: PVC blood bags and dialysis tubes; glass wool = fine glass fibres (heat/sound insulation); flint (lead) glass lenses, prisms; Pyrex labware.
Others: CO2 extinguisher suits electrical fires; ruby = Al2O3 + chromium; Statue of Liberty green = copper patina; alkanes burn to CO2 + water + heat (⚠ APPSC key 2017 gave carbon).
Colloids: blood and milk are colloids; milk = emulsion of fat in water (butter = water in fat); ⚠ APPSC key (2002) gave water dispersed in fat.
Carbon forms and uses: diamond - jewellery, cutting, drilling and grinding tools, glass cutters; graphite - pencil 'lead', dry lubricant, electrodes, reactor moderator, Li-ion battery anodes; coke - fuel and reducing agent in iron extraction; carbon black (lampblack) - pigment in paints, inks, tyres; activated charcoal - adsorbs gases (gas masks), purification; fullerenes and carbon nanotubes - electronics, nanotechnology, drug delivery, lubricants, catalysts; graphene - electronics, composites, sensors, flexible devices.
More polymers: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 = glycine + amino caproic acid (biodegradable); PHBV = 3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid (biodegradable); nylon-6,6 = hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid; terylene = ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid; Buna-S = 1,3-butadiene + styrene; Buna-N = 1,3-butadiene + acrylonitrile.
Electromagnetic induction is used in generators, transformers, induction cooktops, wireless charging and the dynamic microphone (turns sound vibrations into electrical signals).
Refrigerator cycle: the refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside the refrigerator and releases it at the condenser outside.
Osmosis: water (solvent) moves through a semi-permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration (plant roots absorb water this way); in reverse osmosis pressure is applied on the concentrated side, leaving salts and bacteria behind (desalination, water purification).
Bleaching powder releases chlorine, so it is used for water purification and bleaching. Disinfectants (phenol, bleaching powder) are toxic to living tissue, so they are used only on objects; antiseptics (boric acid, iodoform, H2O2) are safe on living tissue.
Soap vs detergent: soap is biodegradable but its alkaline solution harms silk and wool; detergents suit delicate clothes; many older detergents had branched chains that bacteria could not break down, so they were non-biodegradable and caused foam in rivers.
# Smart Materials and Sensors
Hydrogels: up to 99% water; contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery.
Accelerometer (MEMS): triggers airbags, laptop free-fall detection, step counting. MEMS also in gyroscopes, microphones.
Flexible batteries power wearables.
# Transport Technologies
Technology | Fact
FASTag | Passive RFID
Metro card | Passive NFC, 13.56 MHz, ~4 cm
GPS | India's own: NavIC
V2X | C-V2X = 4G/5G; DSRC = Wi-Fi
Hydrogen fuel cell | Emits only water
EVs: PM E-DRIVE scheme (Ministry of Heavy Industries) extended to 31 March 2028.
Black box (flight data recorder + cockpit voice recorder): fitted in the tail to survive crashes ⚠ APPSC key (2004) gave cockpit.
# Positive vs Negative Impacts
Positive | Negative
Communication, flexible work | Decreased privacy
Health tracking | Screen time, eye strain
Digital payments | Cyber fraud, digital divide
Aug 2026: Supreme Court sought Centre's reply on a plea on "high-risk" AI (biometric surveillance, risk-scoring in welfare delivery).
# Number Game and Quick Revision
Item | Fact
Food irradiators (DAE) | 25
Microwave frequency | 2.45 GHz
Ultrasound | >20 kHz
Normal BP | 120/80 mmHg
1 horsepower | 746 W
Lens power | Dioptre = 1/f (m)
## FIRST / LAST / SPECIAL FACTS
Concave lens corrects myopia; convex corrects hypermetropia; car headlight concave mirror, rear-view convex.
Boiling point falls with altitude; salt raises it. Pascal's law - hydraulic brakes; momentum - rockets.
## Everyday Physics and Chemistry Basics
Units: henry = inductance; farad = capacitance; pascal = pressure; decibel = sound level; angstrom = 10^-10 m; light year = distance; picosecond = 10^-12 s.
Instruments: lactometer = milk purity (specific gravity); hygrometer = humidity; barometer = pressure; anemometer = wind speed; atomic (caesium) clock = most exact time.
Optics: silvery crack in glass, diamond sparkle = total internal reflection; rainbow = refraction + dispersion + TIR; sky black in space (no scattering); convex mirror magnification <1.
Radiation: infrared heat therapy for muscular pain; X-rays strongly darken photographic plates; fan under AC lamp seems to reverse (stroboscopic effect).
Mechanics: mass measures inertia; friction opposes motion; doubling momentum makes KE x4 (+300%); no external force = centre-of-mass velocity constant; egg floats in denser salt water.
Electricity: transformer works only on AC; bird on a live wire is safe (no potential difference); unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole.
Heat: tea cools fastest in a metal cup (good conductor); free expansion = into vacuum, no work, ideal-gas temperature unchanged.
Matter: plasma (ionised gas) = 4th state, BEC = 5th; liquid crystals lie between solid and liquid, used in LCD.
Air: inhaled ~21% O2, 78% N2, 0.04% CO2; exhaled ~16% O2, 4% CO2.
Chemistry basics: OIL RIG (oxidation = electron loss); hydrogen = 'inflammable air' (Cavendish 1766), atomic number 1; silicon = 2nd most abundant crustal element after oxygen.
Molecules: chiral = Greek 'hand'; alkaloids contain nitrogen; excess Li makes LiCl pink (F-centres); energy-absorbing reactions = endergonic, energy-releasing = exergonic.
Physics principles: equivalence principle - basis of general relativity, used in GPS time corrections; Doppler principle - red shift of receding galaxies, Doppler ultrasound; Huygens' principle - every point on a wavefront is a source, explains wave propagation, reflection and refraction; Pascal's - hydraulic lift, syringe; Archimedes' - buoyancy; Bernoulli's - wing lift; conservation of momentum - gun recoil, rocket propulsion; conservation of angular momentum - an ice-skater spins faster on pulling in the arms, planetary orbits.
Electrical units: resistance - ohm; resistivity - ohm-metre (ρ = RA/l); conductance (G = 1/R) - siemens, older unit mho; conductivity (1/ρ) - siemens per metre (S/m); elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (1 C = charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons); conventional current flows from positive to negative, opposite to electron flow.
Convex lens (converging): object within F gives a virtual, erect, magnified image (magnifying glass); it forms real images in a camera, compound microscope and telescope; a burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point.
Myopia (short-sightedness): the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina; corrected by a concave lens of negative power.
# Appsc Previous Year Questions
Examination | Question Area
Group 1 Prelims 2024, Paper 2 | Rhodamine B - cotton candy; food additives
APPSC GS 2022 | Ultrasound for foetus (A and R); decreased privacy not a positive impact
APPSC GS 2019 | Dialysis when kidneys fail; food additives added intentionally
# High-probability Mcq Traps
1. Urea is made in the liver, not the kidney.
2. Pellagra = B3, not B5 or C; beri-beri = B1.
3. MRI uses radio waves, no ionising radiation; CT uses X-rays.
4. Additives are intentional; adulterants are harmful.
5. FASTag = RFID; metro card = NFC.
6. C-V2X = 4G/5G, DSRC = Wi-Fi.
7. Bleaching powder is a disinfectant; boric acid, iodoform, H2O2 are antiseptics.
8. Decreased privacy is a negative impact.
9. Fuse is in series; low melting point, high resistivity; ⚠ APPSC key (2012) gave low resistivity.

=== APPSC Prep notes ===
# Food and health terms — definitions and types
Term | Meaning
Dialysis | recommended when the kidneys fail (APPSC-GS 2019); removes wastes and excess water from blood
haemodialysis | machine filter
peritoneal dialysis | peritoneum as membrane
Food additives | chemicals added intentionally during production, processing or storage to improve the qualities of food (APPSC-GS 2019)
Adulteration | intentionally adding inferior/harmful substances
Irradiation | ionising radiation destroys harmful organisms without altering nutrition
Fortification | adding micronutrients
Additive types: preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners, flavour enhancers (MSG)
Adulteration effects: acute poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency
⚠ Additives = added intentionally to improve food; adulterants = inferior/harmful substances
Fortification examples: Iodised salt; rice with iron, folic acid and B12; oil and milk with vitamins A and D; FSSAI "+F" logo
Irradiation features:
Cuts need for chemical additives and refrigeration
Radiolytic products cause negligible chemical change
DAE: 25 food irradiators installed in PPP mode
Gamma rays extend shelf life of potatoes and onions to 8 months without cold storage
General science scope - PYQ practice only: syllabus has no separate general-science section, but APPSC and other exams keep asking basic physics, chemistry, biology and human biology → these questions are filed here
Physics: motion, light, sound, heat, electricity, magnetism, units
Chemistry: elements, compounds, acids and bases, metals, everyday chemicals
Biology: cells, plants, animals, genetics, evolution
Human body: organs, blood, nutrition, vitamins, hormones
# Health devices and imaging → working principle
Imaging | Working principle | Note
X-ray | Ionising EM radiation; dense tissue (bone) absorbs more [GK] | Fractures, chest [GK]
CT scan | Many X-ray images reconstructed by computer into cross-sections [GK] | Higher radiation dose [GK]
MRI | Strong magnetic field + radio waves act on hydrogen nuclei [GK] | No ionising radiation; soft tissue [GK]
Ultrasound | High-frequency sound waves (>20 kHz) and their echoes [GK] | No ionising radiation, so used for foetal development; also detects liver, heart, kidney problems (APPSC-GS 2022, A and R both true, R explains A)
Telemedicine needs: IT fibre backbone + satellite communication
Strongest in: tele-cardiology, pathology, dermatology, radiology + Continuing Medical Education
Status: still nascent in India's public sector
Wearables: give doctors real-time patient data
## Indigenous devices → developer
Device | Developer / place
Chitra heart valve | SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram
Kalam-Raju coronary stent | Dr B. Soma Raju with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Hyderabad
# Household and transport technologies → working principle — Household appliances
## 1. Household appliances
Microwave oven | Microwaves (about 2.45 GHz) make water molecules rotate → heat [GK]
Refrigerator | Vapour-compression cycle: refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside, releases it at the condenser [GK]
Induction cooktop | Electromagnetic induction - eddy currents in a ferromagnetic (iron/steel) vessel [GK]
LED | Electroluminescence at a semiconductor p-n junction [GK]
RO purifier | Pressure applied against osmosis pushes water through a semi-permeable membrane [GK]
Pressure cooker | Higher pressure raises boiling point (to about 120 C) [GK]
Induction stove demand (Mar 2026): rose about three-fold amid LPG shortage fears
# Household and transport technologies → working principle — Smart materials and sensors
## 1. Smart materials and sensors
Material / sensor | Daily application
Hydrogels | Water-absorbing polymers: contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery [GK]
Accelerometer (MEMS) | Senses sudden deceleration to trigger airbags; screen rotation, step counting [GK]
MEMS sensors | Micro-electro-mechanical systems in phone gyroscopes, microphones, pressure sensors [GK]
Graphene oxide sensor | Low-cost flexible sensor with pencil-drawn electrodes (VIS 2026)
Flexible batteries | graphene/carbon-fibre electrodes → power wearables and flexible displays
# Household and transport technologies → working principle — Transport technologies
## 1. Transport technologies
Technology | Principle / fact
FASTag | passive RFID, powered by the reader's field
Metro cards | passive NFC, 13.56 MHz, about 4 cm (2026)
GPS tracking | location-based services; India's own system = NavIC
V2X | TRAI consultation paper prefers C-V2X (uses 4G/5G) vs DSRC (Wi-Fi-based)
Cyber-physical systems | driverless cars, smart factories
Hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles | H2 + O2 → electricity; only water emitted
EVs | lithium-ion battery-driven motors; no tailpipe emission
⚠ C-V2X = 4G/5G; DSRC = Wi-Fi-based
Not in your sources: current central EV incentive scheme and its outlay.
# Food → adulterant; product → harmful chemical
Food | Common adulterant
Milk | Water, detergent, urea, starch [GK]
Turmeric | Metanil yellow, lead chromate [GK]
Mustard oil | Argemone oil (epidemic dropsy) [GK]
Chilli powder | Brick powder, Sudan dyes [GK]
Rhodamine B | Industrial textile dye illegally used to colour cotton candy - Tamil Nadu banned its sale (APPSC-G1 2024)
Aristolochic acid | Aristolochia plants used in some herbal medicines [GK]
BPA (bisphenol A) | Polycarbonate plastics, epoxy linings of food cans, thermal receipts [GK]
Triclosan | Antibacterial soaps, toothpaste, sanitisers [GK]
Lead | Old paints, pipes, some cosmetics, spices adulterated with lead chromate [GK]
Phthalates | Plasticisers in PVC, toys, cosmetics, fragrances [GK]
Distractors in the 2024 PYQ: also carcinogens
benzidine (dye industry)
1,3-butadiene (synthetic rubber)
Exam angle: product → banned chemical matching from recent state bans.
# Schemes, platforms and missions → purpose
Scheme / platform | Purpose / fact
eSanjeevani | national telemedicine service
IHIP | GIS-enabled real-time disease surveillance via Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) of IDSP
Aarogya Setu | contact tracing; used Bluetooth and GPS for COVID-19
National One Health Mission | joins Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and S&T ministries against zoonoses and AMR
PM Kisan Sampada Yojana | MoFPI funds multi-product irradiation units under its Cold Chain scheme; 16 approved, 9 operational (Aug 2025)
Anna Chakra | optimises PDS routes to 4.37 lakh fair price shops; saves about ₹250 crore/yr
NM-ICPS | approved 2018, ₹3,660 crore for 9 years
Geospatial uses in public health:
Disease mapping: hotspots
Contact tracing: e.g. Aarogya Setu
Facility location: siting PHCs/hospitals by population and travel time
AIIMS Mangalagiri: epidemiology unit tracks regional outbreaks + maps NCD indicators
Food safety reforms (Jul 2026):
Food Safety on Wheels
Blockchain batch tracing
"One Nation, One Regulator" → ends dual BIS/AGMARK certification
# Impacts and debates — positive vs negative
Improved communication | Decreased privacy (NOT a positive impact - APPSC-GS 2022)
Flexible working | Screen time, sedentary life, eye strain [GK]
Smarter health tracking (wearables) | Data security and surveillance risks [GK]
Digital payments, e-governance | Digital divide, cyber fraud [GK]
SC plea (Aug 2026): Supreme Court sought Centre's reply on no statutory regime for "high-risk" AI

You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Telecom Technologies – 3G to 5G, 6G Roadmap, Satellite Communication, Optical Fibre

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Telecom Bodies and Milestones
## Bodies → Role
Body | Role
TRAI (1997) | Regulator of telecom and broadcasting
TDSAT (2000 amendment) | Settles telecom disputes; hears appeals against TRAI
C-DOT (1984) | Government telecom R&D centre
TEC | DoT's technical body for standards and equipment testing (not USOF collection)
DoT (1985) | Created when Posts and Telecom split
## Milestones (1980s reforms and FIRSTs)
Year | Event
1975 | India's first experimental satellite telecom
1984 / 1985 / 1986 | C-DOT / DoT / MTNL and VSNL
April 2019 | South Korea: world's first 5G
1 Oct 2022 | India's 5G launch at India Mobile Congress
## EMF Limits for Towers
India (since 2012): one-tenth of ICNIRP limits: 0.92 W/m² at 1800 MHz (ICNIRP: 9.2 W/m²).
APPSC 2021 key gave 9.2 W/m², which is the ICNIRP value, not India's limit.
# Mobile Generations 1G–6G
Generation | Core technology / feature
1G | Analog, FDMA
2G | Digital; GSM (TDMA) and CDMA; SMS
2.5G / 2.75G | GPRS / EDGE (faster GSM data)
3G | Mobile data; CDMA-based (WCDMA/CDMA2000)
4G | LTE, OFDMA; VoLTE = voice over LTE data network
5G | OFDMA; latency as low as 1 ms
6G | Early 2030s; "omnipresent wireless intelligence"
WiMAX = World Wide Interoperability for Microwave Access (IEEE 802.16); wireless data over long distances.

STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: India's Energy Resources and Import Dependence – Crude Oil, Coal, Gas Import Share; Energy Security

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Classification of Energy Resources
Basis | Types
Renewal | Renewable (solar, wind, hydro, biomass, tidal, geothermal) vs non-renewable (coal, oil, gas, nuclear fuels)
Use history | Conventional (fossil fuels, hydro, thermal, biomass/wood) vs non-conventional (solar, tidal, geothermal, nuclear, ocean thermal)
Origin | Not derived from the Sun: geothermal (Earth's interior heat), tidal (movement of ocean water), nuclear (splitting heavy nuclei)
"Conventional" means long-established use, not non-renewable: hydro and biomass are conventional and renewable.
# Domestic Reserves – Number Game
Item | Fact
India's share of world | ~17% of population vs only 0.4% oil, 0.6% gas, 7% coal reserves
Coal | World's fifth-largest reserves; second-largest producer
Sedimentary basins | 26, only 7 producing
Thorium (monazite) | 11.93 Mt monazite with ~1.07 Mt thorium; Andhra Pradesh largest (3.72 Mt), then Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Kerala, West Bengal
Uranium | Modest, mostly low-grade; large low-grade deposit at Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa, AP)
Coal: fifth-largest reserves but second-largest producer.
# Import Dependence and Suppliers
## Fuel-wise Import Share
Fuel | Import share (newest)
Crude oil | 88.5% (PPAC provisional, July 2026)
Natural gas / LNG | ~47–51% (2026); Qatar = key LNG supplier
Coal | ~26% despite being second-largest producer
Lithium | ~90%
LPG | Depends mainly on OMC stocks; semi-strategic underground storage only ~0.14 MT
India = 3rd largest energy consumer and 3rd largest oil consumer (2026).
## Crude Suppliers (2025)
Supplier | Share
Russia (largest in recent years) | ~35%
Iraq | ~20%
Saudi Arabia | ~15%
USA | ~8%
Others: UAE. West Asia + Africa ~65% of supply (Dec 2025).
OPEC ~40% of global oil; its share of India's crude imports below 50% (Aug 2025).
# Oil Consumption Challenges
## Core Challenge
APPSC G2 Mains 2025: core challenge in managing oil consumption = supply-chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices.
Angle | Issue
Price | Global volatility feeds domestic inflation
Fiscal / external | Oil = biggest driver of trade deficit / CAD
Supply route | Chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz
## The 2026 Hormuz Shock
1. Strait of Hormuz (between Iran and Oman) effectively closed by Iran, early March 2026.
2. It carries ~15 million bbl/day (~34% of world crude trade) and a fifth of global LNG.
3. India's crude basket $82.04/bbl (July 2026) vs $70.95 a year earlier; Brent ~$91.84 (Aug 2026).
4. Result: wider trade deficit, inflation, LPG shortage, volatile LNG prices.
5. Refiners ordered under the LPG control order to maximise yield: LPG output 35 → 54 TMT/day in five days.
6. Response: proposed 41 MT strategic fuel programme (Aug 2026).
India's response to the Hormuz closure (2026): India leaned more on domestic coal and gas, and stepped up LNG and LPG purchases from other suppliers such as the US, Oman, Nigeria and Angola.
# Energy Import Bill
Crude import bill FY 2024-25: $137.0 billion (up 3%).
July 2026: $13.7 billion, up 41% year-on-year (PPAC).
Higher oil prices → wider trade deficit and higher inflation.
# Strategic Petroleum Reserves
## Phase I (underground rock caverns)
Site | State | Capacity
Visakhapatnam | Andhra Pradesh | 1.33 MMT
Mangaluru | Karnataka | 1.5 MMT
Padur | Karnataka | 2.5 MMT
Actual stock ~3.37 MT (64% utilisation) → only ~5 days of cover; IEA norm = 90 days (not 60).
## Phase II and New Plan
Phase II approved: Chandikhol (Odisha), Padur (Karnataka); proposed Bikaner (Rajasthan), Rajkot (Gujarat) (Mar 2026).
Proposed decade-long plan (Aug 2026): 41 MT = 28 MT crude + 9 MT LNG + 4 MT LPG; cover ~two months crude, 56 days LNG, six weeks LPG.
Gaps: no underground gas storage; total oil stock ~74 days.
Padur is in both Phase I and Phase II.
Phase I when full: 5.33 MMT would give about 9.5 days of India's crude oil needs.
# Policies – Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 and Upstream
## Hydrocarbon Vision 2025
Long-term hydrocarbon plan adopted in 2000; linked in exams with storage of petroleum products and long-term energy security (UPPSC 2000).
Focus: self-reliance through indigenous production and equity oil abroad; appraisal of all sedimentary basins; free market and competition (no ban on private participation).
## Upstream and Diversification
HELP: single licence for all hydrocarbons; OALP for upstream exploration and production.
One Nation One Gas Grid; domestic E&P plus overseas acreage.
ONGC Videsh (OVL): overseas arm of ONGC; buys equity oil and gas abroad.
2026: refiners + Shipping Corporation of India JV ($1.5–2 bn, 59 ships).
TAPI pipeline: Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India; company TPCL (2014); stalled.
IPI ("peace pipeline"): Iran–Pakistan–India; India moved away (2007–08) towards TAPI.
OALP: Open Acreage Licensing Policy under HELP; companies choose and bid for blocks for upstream exploration and production.
# Import-substitution Fuels
## Methanol Economy (NITI Aayog)
Aims (APPSC G1 2024: all three correct): (i) cut oil import bill, (ii) cut GHG emissions, (iii) convert coal reserves and municipal solid waste into methanol.
Term | Meaning / use
Methanol | Low-carbon, hydrogen-carrier fuel; from biomass, high-ash coal, agri-residue, CO₂ from thermal plants, natural gas
DME (Di-Methyl Ether) | Two methanol molecules minus one water molecule; replaces propane in LPG and diesel in slow-RPM engines
Methanol replaces petrol/diesel in transport, DG sets, boilers, and partly LPG and kerosene in cooking.
Blend | Benefit
M15 (15% methanol in petrol) | At least 15% cut in petrol/crude imports; 20% cut in PM, NOx, SOx
20% DME in LPG | Saves ₹6,000 crore/yr; ₹50–100 per cylinder
## Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP)
Year | Step
January 2003 | 5% EBP in 9 sugarcane States + 4 UTs (incl. Andhra Pradesh)
2013-14 | Blending ~1.53%
ESY 2025-26 | E20 achieved (target advanced from 2030)
1 Apr 2026 | E20 with minimum 95 RON mandated
Farmer payments over ₹1,29,032 crore.
## Compressed Biogas Obligation (CBO) in City Gas Distribution
Year | Share of CNG/PNG
FY 2025-26 / 2026-27 / 2027-28 | 1% / 3% / 4%
From 2028-29 | 5%
Aim: replace LNG imports.
Methanol Economy: the programme is driven by NITI Aayog.
# Demand-side Measures and Partnerships
## EVs and Clean Energy
PM E-DRIVE: from 1 Oct 2024, outlay ₹10,900 crore, replaced FAME-II; extended to March 2028.
NITI's India Electric Mobility Index (4 Aug 2025) and e-Amrit portal.
500 GW non-fossil by 2030 and Green Hydrogen Mission = import-substitution tools; the 41 MT fuel system is a disruption response.
Debate: renewables not yet cutting fossil imports; RE takes years to become firm power while shocks hit at once.
## Energy Partnerships
IEA: India an association country since March 2017; sought full membership (Oct 2023).
Global Biofuels Alliance: launched 9 Sep 2023 at the G20 New Delhi summit; core founders India, USA, Brazil; secretariat in New Delhi.
International Energy Forum (IEF): largest grouping of energy ministers; secretariat in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. India is a member and hosted the 16th IEF Ministerial in New Delhi (April 2018).
# Critical Minerals Security
National Critical Mineral Mission: Cabinet approval 29 Jan 2025; ₹34,300 crore over seven years (₹16,300 crore government + ₹18,000 crore PSUs), to 2030-31.
KABIL (2019): JV of NALCO, HCL and MECL under the Ministry of Mines.
Argentina: KABIL's five lithium blocks in Catamarca (agreement 15 Jan 2024, ~₹200 crore).
# Ap Hydrocarbons
Place | Feature
KG Basin (offshore, East Coast) | Among India's most prolific zones; AP produces gas and crude in the Godavari basin
KG-D6 | Reliance (operator, 66.67%) + BP (33.33%); R-Cluster, Satellites, MJ fields
KG-DWN-98/2 | ONGC deepwater block next to KG-D6
Visakhapatnam | HPCL refinery + Phase I SPR
IIPE Visakhapatnam | Set up 2016, INI 2017; shale-modelling pact with OIL India (Apr 2026)
# Number Game and Quick Revision
Item | Correct Fact
Import share: crude / gas / coal / lithium | 88.5% / ~50% / ~26% / ~90%
World reserve share: oil / gas / coal | 0.4% / 0.6% / 7%
SPR Phase I total | 5.33 MMT (1.33 + 1.5 + 2.5)
SPR actual cover vs IEA norm | ~5 days vs 90 days
Proposed strategic fuel | 41 MT (28 + 9 + 4)

CBO | 1-3-4-5%
## FIRST / LAST / SPECIAL FACTS
First EBP phase: January 2003 (5%).
Largest crude supplier: Russia; key LNG supplier: Qatar.
Only AP SPR: Visakhapatnam (1.33 MMT).
Padur: only site in both SPR phases.
# Appsc Previous Year Questions
Examination | Question Area
Group 2 Mains 2025, Paper 2 | Policy – challenges in managing oil consumption
Group 1 Prelims 2024, Paper 2 | Programme – objectives of the Methanol Economy

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Human Spaceflight - AXIOM-4 and Gaganyaan
## Axiom-4 - Shubhanshu Shukla
Particular | Fact
Launch | 25 June 2025, 12:01 PM IST - Falcon 9 (not Falcon Heavy), Crew Dragon, Launch Complex 39A, Kennedy Space Center, Florida
Mission type | Private Axiom Space mission with NASA and SpaceX (not an ISRO/Roscosmos joint mission)
Indian astronaut | Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla (IAF) - Pilot
Commander | Peggy Whitson (USA); Polish and Hungarian astronauts were Mission Specialists
Stay on ISS | 25 June - 15 July 2025; docking 26 June 2025, 4:30 PM IST after a 28-hour journey
Science | 60 studies from 31 countries; India - 7 ISRO-selected microgravity experiments, 5 ISRO-NASA joint studies, 2 in-orbit STEM demos
Delays | Original date 29 May 2025; LOX leak, Zvezda module snag; quarantine from 25 May
Shukla = first Indian on the ISS and first Indian in space in 40 years - after Rakesh Sharma (Soyuz T-11, 1984).
Axiom-4 flew on Falcon 9 (not Falcon Heavy); it was a private Axiom mission, not ISRO-Roscosmos.
## Gaganyaan - IADT-1 and Roadmap
IADT-1 - ISRO's first Integrated Air Drop Test (August 2025): validated the parachute-based deceleration system of the Gaganyaan crew module; a ~5-tonne dummy crew capsule was dropped from an IAF Chinook helicopter; main parachutes deployed in sequence.
IADT-1 was not an orbital flight - uncrewed orbital flights are G1 onwards.
Done (MoS Jitendra Singh): propulsion systems, ECLSS engineering model, Crew Escape System (five types of motors, TV-D1 precursor); HS200 motors; C32-G stage. Next: TV-D2, then G1 (uncrewed).
Milestone | Target
Crewed Gaganyaan flight | Q1 2027
Bharatiya Antariksh Station | 2035
Indian Moon landing | 2040
Upcoming missions: Gaganyaan, Chandrayaan-4, Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
# Isro, Space Infrastructure and Space Law
## Chandrayaan-2's CHACE-2
CHACE-2 (Chandra's Atmospheric Composition Explorer-2) on the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, developed by ISRO's Space Physics Laboratory.
First-ever direct observation of a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) impact on the lunar exosphere - dayside exosphere density rose by more than one order of magnitude (sodium, potassium, argon knocked off the regolith).
Chandrayaan-2: launched 22 July 2019 on GSLV Mk-III-M1; eight payloads; Vikram lander failed, orbiter operational.
LUPEX - India-Japan lunar mission.
## Second Launch Complex - Kulasekarapattinam
Location | Kulasekarapattinam, Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district, Tamil Nadu - ~2,300 acres
For | SSLV only - PSLV/GSLV stay at Sriharikota (AP)
Completion / first launch | December 2026 / Q4 2026
Capacity | 20-25 launches a year
Foundation | Foundation stone by PM Modi via video, February 2024; bhumi puja by ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan
## National Space Day and the Space-Law Gap
Second National Space Day: 23 August 2025 - marks the Chandrayaan-3 soft landing near the lunar south pole.
India has ratified the UN space treaties but has no comprehensive national space law (no Space Activities Act); IN-SPACe works without statutory authority.
Existing framework: Catalogue of Indian Standards for Space Industry (safety); Indian Space Policy (2023); IN-SPACe Norms, Guidelines and Procedures (NPG), 2023 - authorisation of commercial activities.
Outer Space Treaty (1967): space the "province of all mankind"; Article VI - the state is responsible for private activities; treaties are not self-executing.
Countries with national space laws: Japan, Luxembourg, US.
## Protecting India's Satellites - "Bodyguard Satellites"
IS4OM - Indian Space Situational Awareness and Management Centre, Bengaluru; Project NETRA; Multi-Object Tracking Radar at Sriharikota; 10+ collision-avoidance manoeuvres in 2023.
Cyber: CERT-In guidelines (2025); IN-SPACe licensing; lesson from the 2022 Viasat cyberattack (Ukraine).
Space weather: Aditya-L1; CESSI (IISER Kolkata).
Debris: pledge of "Debris-Free Space Missions by 2030" at the 2024 IADC meet (hosted by India). Norms: UN COPUOS guidelines (2019).
Fleet: ₹27,000 crore programme for ~52 surveillance satellites from 2026.
# World Space and Astronomy
## Solar Missions
Mission | Fact
Solar Orbiter (ESA-NASA, launched February 2020) | First spacecraft to image the Sun's poles; first to trace Solar Energetic Electrons (SEE) to solar flares (bursts) and CMEs (gradual release); 300+ SEE bursts studied (2020-22)
Parker Solar Probe (NASA, 2018) | Closest approach to the Sun
Aditya-L1 (ISRO, 2023) | India's first solar observatory at Lagrange Point L1
Sun's magnetic (solar) cycle: 11 years.
## Stars and Physics
UPM J1040-3551 AabBab - rare quadruple system: two cold T-type brown dwarfs orbiting a pair of young red dwarfs - first such arrangement seen (Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, Sept 2025).
Brown dwarfs - "failed stars": cannot sustain hydrogen fusion; up to 70 times Jupiter's mass; companion chance below 5%.
Red dwarfs - most common stars (about 70% of Milky Way stars); long-lived. Blue supergiants are among the hottest, most luminous stars - not cold.
Entangled atomic clocks (Jacob Covey, Igor Pikovski, Johannes Borregaard; PRX Quantum, July 2025) - tabletop test of the quantum-gravity interface with three entangled ytterbium clocks at different elevations; entanglement in a W state (robust to particle loss, unlike GHZ); frequency shift ~0.02 Hz for 1 km; coherence time ~50 s.
Quantum gravity theory | Idea
String Theory | Extra dimensions and gravitons
Loop Quantum Gravity | Discrete spacetime at the Planck scale
# Navy - Warships, Fleet Reviews and Sailing Expeditions
## INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri (AP Angle)

# Health - Vaccines, Therapies and Diseases
## AdFalciVax
India's first indigenous multi-stage malaria vaccine (licensed) - recombinant chimeric vaccine against *Plasmodium falciparum*; acts before the parasite enters the bloodstream.
Developed by ICMR-Regional Medical Research Centre, Bhubaneswar using *Lactococcus lactis*, with ICMR-NIMR and NII, New Delhi; stable over 9 months at room temperature.
## CAR T-cell Therapy
CAR = Chimeric Antigen Receptor - the patient's own T-cells (not B-cells) engineered to attack cancer.
Approved for blood cancers - ALL, Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, Multiple Myeloma; not yet solid tumours.
Side effects: Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), ICANS (neurotoxicity). Cost abroad over ₹3-4 crore per patient.
NexCAR19 - India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy (blood cancer); CDSCO approval 2023. IIT Bombay + Tata Memorial Centre - India's first cost-effective platform "InCART"; DBT supports Make-in-India CAR-T.
Dual-targeting CAR-T (BCMA + CD19) for multiple myeloma - co-developed with the Technology Development Board (18 May 2026).

## From GM to Genome-Edited Crops
Bt cotton - India's only commercial GM crop.
GM vs GE: GM inserts foreign genes (transgenic); GE edits the plant's own genes, no foreign DNA.
GE rice variety | Developer | Parent
DRR Rice 100 (Kamala) | ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad | Samba Mahsuri (BPT-5204)
Pusa DST Rice 1 | ICAR-IARI, New Delhi | Cotton Dora Sannalu (MTU 1010)
Edit | Benefit
Samba Mahsuri - Gn1a (cytokinin oxidase) edited | More spikelets, ~19% yield gain
MTU-1010 | Drought and salt tolerance (saline/alkaline soils)
Mustard (GE) | Canola-quality, low pungency, disease/pest resistance (2nd-year trials, possible release 2026)
Technology: CRISPR-Cas9; claimed 17-30% higher yield, 20 days earlier maturity, drought/salinity tolerance; non-transgenic.
Criticism: Coalition for a GM-Free India analysed AICRIP (2023-24) data - Pusa DST Rice 1 equal/lower yield in 12 of 20 sites; Kamala underperformed in 8 of 19; Kamala flowering 101 vs 104 days.
Regulation: March 2022 MoEFCC OM - transgene-free GE plants exempt from GM biosafety rules; need IBSC certification (not GEAC). DBT guidelines (2022) - gene-edited crops without foreign DNA not treated as GMOs; oversight RCGM and GEAC.
Funding: National Agricultural Science Fund (~2018); ₹500 crore in Union Budget 2023-24. ICAR mapped ~178 genes in 24 field crops and 43 genes in horticultural crops.
Tools: Cas9, Cas12a; newer GeoCas9 and CasLambda supplied by the Innovative Genomics Institute (founded by Jennifer Doudna) - training at IARI (Feb 2025); indigenous TnpB-based mini genome editor - team of Kutubuddin Ali Molla, Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack; 9 scientists trained abroad, 12 more scheduled.
Transgene-free GE plants need only IBSC certification, not GEAC approval.
## Asgard Archaea (IISc Study)
IISc Bengaluru (The EMBO Journal) - Odinarchaeota (an Asgard archaea) has two FtsZ genes plus a tubulin-like gene.
OdinFtsZ1 - straight protofilaments, anchors directly to membranes (bacteria-like); OdinFtsZ2 - spiral ring-like structures, needs adaptor proteins. Methods: phylogenetics, cryo-electron microscopy.
Asgard archaea - named after Norse gods (Odin-, Loki-, Thorarchaeota); deep-sea sediments; closest living relatives of eukaryotes.
FtsZ - bacterial division protein forming the Z-ring; tubulin is the eukaryotic hallmark (not unique to bacteria).

# High-probability Mcq Traps
1. Axiom-4 = Falcon 9 (not Falcon Heavy), private Axiom mission; Shukla was Pilot, Peggy Whitson Commander.
2. IADT-1 tested parachutes - it was not an orbital flight; next are TV-D2 and G1.
3. Kulasekarapattinam is for SSLV only; PSLV/GSLV stay at Sriharikota.
4. IN-SPACe has no statutory authority; India has no national space law.
5. INS Tamal - last foreign-built warship, Western Fleet, not the first BrahMos ship.
6. IASV Triveni was built at Puducherry, not Goa; Bright Star began in 1980, not 2005; France was not in Bright Star 2025.
7. IADWS (QRSAM + VSHORADS + laser DEW) is fully indigenous - not with Rafael.
8. Vikram 3201 = VSSC + SCL Chandigarh, not under the Semicon India Programme. 4G stack: RAN = Tejas Networks, Core = C-DOT, integration = TCS.
9. CAR-T uses T-cells (not B-cells), approved only for blood cancers; PAM is not communicable and not spread by drinking water.
10. Tubulin is eukaryotic (FtsZ is bacterial); transgene-free GE plants need IBSC, not GEAC; SARAL makes research summaries, it is not funding.

## 1. Systems
System | How it works | Examples / use

RHU (Radioisotope Heater Unit) | Heat only — ⚠ no electricity | Keeps instruments from freezing
Fission reactor | Controlled chain reaction → much higher power | Lunar/Martian habitats
Nuclear Thermal Propulsion (NTP) | Reactor heats liquid hydrogen propellant | ~twice efficiency of chemical rockets
Nuclear Electric Propulsion (NEP) | Electricity accelerates ionised propellant | Low thrust, very high efficiency
Radioisotope systems used since 1961; Voyager launched 1977 (5-year mission), now >20 billion km away

You check the answer keys of previous-year exam questions (PYQs: APPSC, UPSC, other state PSCs, SSC) for an APPSC exam-preparation app. For each PYQ you get the question, its numbered options and the key the app currently gives. Judge the key ONLY against the study notes supplied in the message (several apps' notes on the same topic). Do not use outside knowledge to overrule the notes; if the notes do not settle it, say so.

For every PYQ return one result:
- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". Also use CONFLICT when the notes contradict each other on this exact point (option = what the stronger/more specific note says; say "notes disagree" in evidence).
- NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED). For "which is NOT correct", "wrong pair" and statement-combination questions, work out which option the notes make right before judging. Keep evidence under 30 words; leave it empty for AGREE. Return exactly one result per PYQ id, in order.

STUDY NOTES

TOPIC: Sep–4 Nov 2026: Environment in news - reports, indices, species, protected areas, climate negotiations

=== APPSC Complete notes ===
# Tiger Reserves and Ca|ts Accreditation
## Nameri Tiger Reserve
Nameri TR: Sonitpur, Assam; National Park since 1998; river Jia Bhoroli; now CA|TS Approved.
Nameri Wild Classroom: launched by the Assam Forest Department; experiential conservation education for students from Class 8 onwards.
Kaziranga and Manas are UNESCO sites.
## CA|TS - Conservation Assured | Tiger Standards
Launched at the 1st Asian Parks Congress, Japan, 2013.
7 pillars, 17 elements (first 5 pillars = CA, last 2 = TS).
India now has 24 CA|TS-accredited tiger reserves; Assam has 4.
State | Accredited tiger reserves
Assam | Manas, Kaziranga, Orang, Nameri
Madhya Pradesh | Satpura, Pench, Kanha, Panna, Bandhavgarh
Maharashtra | Pench, Melghat, Tadoba-Andhari, Navegaon-Nagzira
West Bengal | Sundarbans
The current count of CA|TS-accredited reserves is 24, not 15. Pench appears twice (MP and Maharashtra).
## Tiger Background
Item | Fact
Project Tiger | 1 April 1973 (9 reserves)
NTCA | 2006
AITE 2022 | 3,682 tigers (estimate); 3,167 = camera-trapped minimum; 1,411 in 2006
Top States (2022) | MP 785, Karnataka 563, Uttarakhand 560
Tiger reserves area | 84,488 sq km (~2.6% of India)
Global Tiger Day | 29 July
IUCN status | Endangered
# Species Conservation - Snow Leopard, Gib, Stubble
## Snow Leopard Safari, Leh
India's first high-altitude Snow Leopard Safari: launched 7 October 2026, Leh, Ladakh, during Wildlife Week.
LG Vinai Kumar Saxena flagged off 6 open-back vehicles.
Implemented by SHAN Society (Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation) + Ladakh Forest Department.
SPAI 2024: India 718 snow leopards; Ladakh 477 (highest).
*Panthera uncia*; IUCN Vulnerable; WPA Schedule I; CITES Appendix I.
State animal of Himachal Pradesh; UT animal of Ladakh.
International Snow Leopard Day: 23 October; Project Snow Leopard: 2009.
Ladakh UT since 31 October 2019.
## Great Indian Bustard
Union Environment Minister released two captive-bred male GIBs at Sam, Desert National Park, near Jaisalmer.
Desert NP: Thar Desert; over 3,160 sq km; rainfall under 100 mm; Jurassic fossils; extinct salt-lake beds.
GIB: *Ardeotis nigriceps*; IUCN Critically Endangered; Rajasthan State Bird; main threat power lines.
Snow leopard | Vulnerable | Leh safari
Great Indian Bustard | Critically Endangered | Desert NP
## Haryana's Parali Protection Force
Set up before the paddy harvest: field surveillance, drone monitoring, midnight patrols at district and block level.
Alternatives promoted: Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, mulching, composting, biomass use.
Crop-residue burning emits PM2.5, PM10, CO.
Stubble burning (2025 vs 2021): down 93% Punjab, 91% Haryana; CAQM mandates 5-10% biomass co-firing.
Haryana formed 1 November 1966; capital Chandigarh.
## Maharashtra's New Protected Areas (31 Oct 2026)
26th State Board for Wildlife meeting chaired by CM Devendra Fadnavis.
Kolamarka Conservation Reserve and expanded Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary area to be designated wildlife sanctuaries; 14 new Conservation Reserves across seven districts.
Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972: Section 6 State Boards chaired by CMs; Section 36A Conservation Reserves; Section 26A final notification of sanctuaries.
Tansa is linked to the Tansa Reservoir.
# New Species Discovered
Species | Type | Place | Institution / note
*Hemidactylus cairnicola* | Gecko | Nalgonda, Telangana | ZSI; named for stone cairns
*Hemidactylus koyaorum* | Gecko | Pakhal WLS, Warangal, Telangana | ZSI; honours the Koya tribe
*Didymocarpus nautiyalii* | Herb, family Gesneriaceae | Shi-Yomi, Arunachal Pradesh | Honours Prof. Sunil Nautiyal, former Director, G.B. Pant NIHE (Almora; MoEFCC)
*Rhysida quadrispinosa, R. coorgensis, R. neyyarensis* | Centipedes | Western Ghats (Kerala, Karnataka) | ZSI Western Ghats Regional Centre + Malabar Christian College, Kozhikode
*Osbeckia assamensis* | Plant, family Melastomataceae | Manas National Park | Namita Nath (Gauhati University) + Barnali Das (Pragjyotish College)
*Ophiorrhiza shidiensis, O. pemae* | Flowering plants, family Rubiaceae (coffee family) | Vijaynagar, Changlang, Arunachal | BSI + Madras Christian College, Chennai
*Dicharax tilariensis* | Microscopic land snail | Tilari, Kolhapur, Maharashtra | Endemic; second species of genus Dicharax
Telangana geckos: Telangana's endemic reptiles now 6.
D. nautiyalii: herb about 8 cm; leathery leaves, blue-violet flowers; on moist rocks above 1,000 m.
[23 Oct 2026] Centipedes: published in International Journal of Tropical Insect Science; India's Rhysida species now 23; centipedes = class Chilopoda, phylum Arthropoda.
[30 Oct 2026] Osbeckia assamensis: surveys 2021-2025; published in Phytotaxa; Manas lies near the India-Bhutan border; UNESCO World Heritage Site 1985, also a Tiger Reserve and Biosphere Reserve.
[31 Oct 2026] Ophiorrhiza: published in Taiwania on 23 Oct 2026; BSI est. 1890, HQ Kolkata, under MoEFCC; Arunachal capital Itanagar.
[02 Nov 2026] Dicharax tilariensis: lives in moist soil and leaf litter of semi-evergreen forests; genus restricted to the northern Western Ghats; snails = phylum Mollusca, class Gastropoda.
ZSI: est. 1916, HQ Kolkata. Western Ghats: UNESCO site 2012; spread over Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu.
BSI = 1890; ZSI = 1916; both HQ Kolkata.
# Air Quality - Swachh Vayu Survekshan and Ncap
## Clean Air Day
International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies: 7 September; designated by UNGA in 2019; first observed 2020; India marks it as Swachh Vayu Diwas.
## Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026 (5th edition)
Launched 2022-23 by MoEFCC; covers 130 NCAP cities.
5th awards on 7 Sep 2026 (Clean Air Day).
Category | 2025 winner | 2026 winner
Category-1 (10 lakh+) | Indore | Lucknow (198/200, ₹1.5 crore); Indore 2nd, Jabalpur 3rd
Category-2 (3-10 lakh) | Amravati | Rourkela (198.5); Guntur joint 2nd
Category-3 (under 3 lakh) | Dewas | Kalinganagar
Municipal wards included for the first time in 2026 (7,400+ wards): Lucknow Zone-4 Ward-70 1st (wards over 30,000), Bhopal Ward-60 2nd, Nashik Ward-7 3rd; also Wards 30 and 36 Bhubaneswar, Ward 13 Rourkela.
Jammu Municipal Corporation recognised in all 3 ward categories (₹50 lakh).
AP angle: Guntur was joint 2nd in the 3-10 lakh category, 2026.
## NCAP Progress
NCAP: launched 2019; 130 cities in 24 States/UTs; tracked on the PRANA portal.
Grants 2019-20 to 2025-26: ₹16,423.55 crore; utilised ₹11,575.54 crore (70.5%).
2025-26 vs 2017-18: 108 of 130 cities lowered PM10; 72 cut over 20%; 26 cut over 40%; only 14 met the PM10 NAAQS (60 µg/m³).
2025-26: 65 cities within the PM2.5 limit (40 µg/m³); Delhi 102 µg/m³.
SAMEER app: AQI for 292+ cities; network (Mar 2026): 1,646 stations in 603 cities.
## AQI, GRAP and Laws
AQI: 6 categories, 8 pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, lead; methane not included); the worst sub-index decides; Very Poor 301-400; Severe 401-500.
GRAP: 4 stages, from Poor (201-300) to Severe Plus (over 450).
Law / tool | Year
Water Act (CPCB set up) | 1974
Air Act | 1981
NAAQS (12 pollutants) | 2009
NGT Act | 2010
National AQI | 2015
GRAP (Delhi-NCR) | 2017
CAQM Act | 2021
CPCB industry classes: 419 sectors = 125 Red, 137 Orange, 94 Green, 54 White, 9 Blue.
OCEMS mandatory for 17 categories of highly polluting industries.
Delhi: only BS-VI/CNG/electric buses from 1 Nov 2026; particulate norm 50 mg/Nm³ from 1 Oct 2026.
PM10 = particles 10 micrometres or smaller.
Greening: Nagar Van Yojana target 1,000 by 2026-27 (626 supported); Aravalli Green Wall 6.31 million ha; Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 262.4 crore saplings (Dec 2025).
[25 Oct 2026] AATAL: world's first integrated air pollution analysis centre for Delhi-NCR (Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory); inaugurated by MoS (IC) Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh; identifies pollution sources in real time, analyses chemical composition, toxicity and health impacts; supports source apportionment and forecasts. CPCB est. 1974, HQ New Delhi.
[22 Oct 2026] Green Diwali campaign: by WWF-India, in line with Mission LiFE; urges avoiding firecrackers (air and noise pollution); runs till 8 Nov 2026; awareness in schools, colleges, RWAs. WWF est. 1961, HQ Gland; WWF-India est. 1969, HQ New Delhi; Mission LiFE launched by PM Modi on 20 Oct 2022 at Kevadia, Gujarat.
CPCB categories by pollution: Red is the most polluting, then Orange and Green; White is the least polluting (practically non-polluting); Blue is for essential environmental services such as waste treatment.
# Short-lived Climate Pollutants and the Ozone Treaties
## SLCPs
SLCPs cause up to 45% of present warming; IPCC: rapid cuts can avoid up to 0.6°C by 2050.
Also called super pollutants / Short-Lived Climate Forcers.
Major warming SLCPs: black carbon, methane, tropospheric ozone, HFCs; sulphate aerosols cool.
Black carbon is not a greenhouse gas: a particle that absorbs radiation.
Tropospheric ozone is not directly emitted: formed from methane, NOx, VOCs in sunlight.
Methane: about 80 times CO2's warming over 20 years; second-largest contributor after CO2.
Stratospheric ozone ~10-50 km; tropospheric ozone surface to 10 km.
Ozone causes loss of about 110 million tonnes of staple crops a year; air pollution about 7 million premature deaths a year globally.
India: air pollution caused 1.67 million deaths in 2019 (17.8%); loss US$36.8 billion (1.36% of GDP).
India's methane (2016, Third BUR): Agriculture 73.96%, Waste 14.46%, Energy 10.62%, Industry 0.96%.
India's measures: PMUY (over 10.5 crore LPG connections), GOBARdhan, SRI, DSR, alternate wetting and drying.
India has NOT joined the Global Methane Pledge; it calls farm methane "survival emissions".
## International Instruments
Instrument | Fact
Vienna Convention | 1985
Montreal Protocol | Adopted 16 Sep 1987, in force 1 Jan 1989; ozone-depleting substances; Ozone Day 16 September
Kigali Amendment | Adopted 15 Oct 2016 at Kigali, Rwanda; in force 1 Jan 2019; legally binding HFC phase-down; can avoid up to 0.5°C by 2100
Global Methane Pledge | COP26 Glasgow 2021; cut 30% from 2020 levels by 2030; 159 countries + EC; India not a member
Climate and Clean Air Coalition | UNEP-led; India joined 2019
[21 Oct 2026] Kigali Amendment completes 10 years: implemented under the UNEP Ozone Secretariat with the Multilateral Fund; India ratified Sep 2021; India freezes HFCs by 2028, begins phase-down from 2032 and cuts 85% by 2047; HFCs do not deplete ozone; UNEP est. 1972, HQ Nairobi.
# Climate Negotiations and Climate Reports
[19 Oct 2026] COP31: 31st Conference of the Parties, 9-20 Nov 2026, Expo Center, Antalya, Turkiye; Turkiye host country, Australia to lead negotiations.
UNFCCC: adopted 1992 (Rio Earth Summit), in force 21 Mar 1994; secretariat Bonn, Germany.
Paris Agreement: adopted at COP21 (2015), in force 4 Nov 2016; aims well below 2°C while pursuing 1.5°C; NDCs = national climate commitments under it.
[25 Oct 2026] UNEP 17th Emissions Gap Report 2026 "The Point of Return":
Global GHG emissions 58.4 Gt CO2e in 2025, down only 0.1 Gt from 2024.
Temporary overshoot of 1.5°C unavoidable without rapid cuts; low-overshoot pathway 1.7-1.8°C, with about 50% chance of returning to 1.5°C by 2100.
Needs cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040 (vs 2025).
New NDCs (about two-thirds of countries) cut only 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035.
[29 Oct 2026] UNFCCC NDC report: even with full NDC implementation, emissions fall only 9% by 2035 from 2019 levels; commitments insufficient for 1.5°C; strong cuts could limit peak warming to about 1.8°C.
[18 Oct 2026] Tuvalu: rising sea levels may make parts uninhabitable by the end of the century; formerly Ellice Islands; Polynesian country between Australia and Hawaii; about 26 sq km, world's fourth-smallest country; nine islands (four reef islands, five atolls) incl. Nanumanga, Niutao, Niulakita; Kiribati to north, Fiji to south; capital Funafuti; no rivers; revenue from copra, postage stamps, fishing licences; currency Australian Dollar.
Emissions Gap Report | UNEP | 17th, "The Point of Return"
NDC Synthesis | UNFCCC | 9% fall by 2035
# Biodiversity Conventions, Ramsar and Forests
## CBD COP17 (19-31 Oct 2026)
[04 Nov 2026] Held at Meridian Expo & Event Centre, Yerevan, Armenia; theme "Taking Action for Nature"; chaired by Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan.
Nearly 50 decisions on the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF).
Indian delegation led by Bhupender Yadav; highlighted 23 national targets and 142 indicators in the updated NBSAP.
Logo: butterfly *Polyommatus eriwanensis* (Eriwan Blue) with 23 colours for 23 targets.
Adopted the Yerevan Pathway and Sevan Guidelines; about US$2 billion pledged; Biodiversity Bond and Investment Incubator.
COP18: Quito, Ecuador, 2028.
CBD: adopted at 1992 Rio Summit, in force 29 Dec 1993, Secretariat Montreal. KMGBF: adopted at COP15 Montreal 2022; 4 goals for 2050, 23 targets for 2030.
## Ramsar Sites Rise to 103 (20 Oct 2026)
Announced by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav: Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh) added; India now 103 Ramsar sites.
Ramsar Convention: adopted 2 Feb 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; in force 1975; India joined 1 Feb 1982; first Indian sites Chilika Lake and Keoladeo NP (1981); secretariat Gland, Switzerland; World Wetlands Day 2 February; Tamil Nadu has the most Ramsar sites.
Tso Kar: Ladakh launched restoration of the shrinking Tso Kar ("White Lake") on the Rupshu Plateau; high-altitude saline lake-wetland complex in southeastern Ladakh; habitat of the Black-necked Crane; Tso Kar Wetland Complex (Tso Kar + Startsapuk Tso) = Ramsar 2020.
Bhitarkanika (Odisha): Ramsar; estuarine crocodiles.
## Kerala's Red List of Ecosystems (20 Oct 2026)
India's first state-level Red List Assessment of Ecosystems: by Kerala State Biodiversity Board (KSBB, est. 2005 under the Biological Diversity Act 2002); one-year study of all 14 districts, funded by KSBB; uses the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems method (risk of ecosystem collapse).
IUCN: est. 1948, HQ Gland, Switzerland.
## Coral Reefs (28 Oct 2026)
IUCN: 96% of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems at risk of collapse by 2075; assessment covered about 188,362 sq km, nearly all rated 'Critically Endangered'.
Threats: climate change, warming, overfishing, coastal development, pollution, acidification.
India's reef regions: Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Lakshadweep, Andaman-Nicobar.
## FAO COFO 28 (4 Nov 2026)
COFO 28 held in Rome, 28 Sep-2 Oct 2026, with the 10th World Forest Week; theme "Forests for food, resilience and prosperity"; chaired by Pierre Taty (Republic of the Congo); 128 member countries; India represented by MoEFCC.
India's forest and tree cover: 82.74 million ha, 25.17% of geographical area.
FAO released "The State of the World's Forests 2026: Restoring Forests and Landscapes - The Way Forward for a Sustainable Future": about 1.56 billion ha degraded, nearly 10% of world land, about 5.2 times India's area.
FAO: est. 16 Oct 1945, HQ Rome; World Food Day 16 October; COFO = FAO's highest forestry body, meets every two years.
National Forest Policy 1988: target 33% cover; NDC: extra carbon sink of 2.5-3 billion tonnes CO2e by 2030.
IUCN, WWF and Ramsar secretariat are all at Gland, Switzerland; CBD secretariat is Montreal; UNFCCC is Bonn.
Living Planet Report 2026 (October 2026): by WWF with the Zoological Society of London (ZSL); title "The Science of Hope"; monitored wildlife populations fell by an average of 73% (1970-2022); steepest fall in freshwater (85%), then terrestrial (69%) and marine (59%).
# Coasts, Mangroves and Oceans
## National Coastal Mission 2.0
Guidelines released by the Union MoEFCC Minister, New Delhi.
2025-26 to 2030-31; ₹767 crore; Central Sector Scheme; 9 coastal States + 4 UTs; directly administered by MoEFCC.
Integrates NCM 1.0 (2021-22 to 2025-26); framework for Marine Spatial Planning, climate resilience, marine pollution, Blue Economy.
## Pichavaram Mangroves (Tamil Nadu) - Valuation
Study: Economic Valuation and Blue Carbon Assessment of Ecosystem Services in the Pichavaram Mangrove Forest.
Total Economic Value ₹2,485.38 crore (~₹1.83 crore/hectare); survey of 302 households in 5 villages.
Service | Value
Soil organic carbon | ₹1,224.63 crore (largest)
Carbon stock in vegetation | ₹387.77 crore
Oxygen regulation | ₹181.22 crore
Coastal protection | ₹147.17 crore
Vegetation carbon 79.449 t/ha (~291.33 t CO2/ha); soil organic carbon 251.14 t/ha; combined carbon value ₹1,612.40 crore.
Most mangrove carbon is below ground, in sediments.
## Mangrove Background
ISFR 2023: mangrove cover 4,992 sq km (~0.15% of area; 4,628 in 2013); West Bengal > Gujarat > A&N Islands.
IUCN 2024: 50% of the world's mangrove ecosystems at risk of collapse.
MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes): 2023, ₹100 crore.
Adaptations: pneumatophores, prop roots, vivipary; mangroves = "Kidneys of the Planet".
Sundarbans: largest; Royal Bengal Tiger.
## Offshore Nodule Blocks near Great Nicobar
Ministry of Mines notified 2 offshore blocks for composite licences (nodules and crusts): West Sewell Ridge-01 (Andaman Sea) 1,000 sq km + Sewell Rise-01 632 sq km = 1,632 sq km.
Great Nicobar also has a ₹72,000-crore project (transshipment port, airport, power plant, 2 cities).
Polymetallic nodules: nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper, REEs; ISA zones Clarion-Clipperton (off Mexico), Central Indian Ocean Basin, Peru Basin. Polymetallic sulphides: copper, zinc, lead, silver, gold.
ISA sulphide contracts: 2016 (Central Indian Ridge, Southwest Indian Ridge) and Sep 2025: India first country with two ISA sulphide contracts; executed by NCPOR, Goa (est. 1998).
EEZ: 200 nm (~370 km) under UNCLOS; seabed beyond = common heritage of mankind.
Offshore Areas Mineral (D&R) Act, 2002; India coastline 11,098 km; UN Ocean Decade 2021-2030.
Deep Ocean Mission: 2021, ₹4,077 crore (MoES); Samudrayaan = manned deep-sea mission under it (2021-2026).
Sagar Manthan research vessel: launched by GRSE on 9 September for NCPOR; 89.5 m, 5,900 GT; ₹840 crore; built at Rishi Bankim Shipyard, Kolkata; operational 2028; surveys to 6 km depth; for the equatorial Indian Ocean, Bay of Bengal, Antarctic waters.
A composite licence does not mean immediate mining.
Pichavaram: a mangrove forest in Tamil Nadu (Cuddalore district, near Chidambaram).
# Disasters, Cyclones and Natural Phenomena
## Nepal Disaster, 26 Aug 2026
1. Rock-ice collapse near the Nepal-China border; material plunged about 1 km.
2. Initially read as a 4.4-magnitude quake; USGS said the signal came from the collapse (energy ~magnitude 5.2).
3. A rock-ice collapse-triggered debris flood, not a conventional GLOF; flash floods on the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli rivers.
4. Toll (NDRRMA, 8 September 2026): 1,357 dead, 5,326 unaccounted for – it rose from a few hundred in the first days; 93,000+ need assistance; Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims missing.
Source of the flood: an ice-rock avalanche from the northern slopes of Mt Langtang Lirung into the Lhende River, which feeds the Bhotekoshi.
5. Nepal lost about 475 MW hydropower; 13 hydropower projects damaged.
6. China: Gyirong Port (Tibet) buried (upgraded at $175.8 million).
7. India: rivers Gandak, Kosi, Ganga; Bihar and UP alert; Valmikinagar Barrage watched (not Farakka); Maharajganj, Kushinagar; India sent 47.5 tonnes of relief.
## India's Himalayan Hazard Measures
National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme: ₹150 crore; Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand.
NDMA Guidelines on GLOFs: 2020; Dam Safety Act: 2021.
National Landslide Risk Mitigation Project: ₹1,000 crore, 15 States.
Vasundhara Lake, Chamoli: Uttarakhand's first real-time GLOF early warning system; monitors water level, weather, snow depth, flow, seismic activity; satellite communication (no mobile network); solar-powered. Uttarakhand capital Dehradun, summer capital Gairsain.
## Cyclones
[26 Oct 2026] Cyclone Arnab: name proposed by Bangladesh; formed in the Bay of Bengal; 'Arnab' = ocean/sea in Bengali; intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and was expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam on 28 Oct 2026 (AP angle).
Naming: WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones (13 members, 13 names each; current list adopted April 2020); RSMC New Delhi (IMD) names North Indian Ocean cyclones; a name is assigned at 34 knots (~63 km/h), sequentially, not by landfall country.
Terms: hurricane (North Atlantic, NE/Central North Pacific), typhoon (NW Pacific), 'willy-willy' (historical Australian term).
[02 Nov 2026] Cyclone 'Murasu': India-proposed; Tamil word for a large war drum used to announce wars, victories and royal orders (public alertness); previous cyclone Arnab (Bangladesh); next names Akvan (Iran), Kani (Maldives), Elgaman (Oman), Seil (Oman), Sahab (Pakistan).
Other Indian names: Aag, Vyom, Jhar, Probaho, Neer, Prabhanjan, Ghurni, Ambud, Jaladhi, Vega.
Panel members (13): Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, UAE, Yemen.
WMO est. 1950, HQ Geneva; IMD est. 1875, under Ministry of Earth Sciences (Dr. Jitendra Singh).
Other disasters: Qeshm Island oil spill (Iran); Cyclone Ditwah (Sri Lanka); Bald Range wildfire (Canada).
## Volcanoes, Earthquakes and Glaciers
Event | Place | Fact
[16 Oct 2026] Mount Kanlaon | Negros Island, Visayas, Philippines | Ash and smoke up to 6 km; active stratovolcano
[01 Nov 2026] Mayon | Albay Province, Luzon, Philippines | Lava, smoke, ash; Daraga town evacuated; nearly symmetrical stratovolcano; monitored by PHIVOLCS
Anak Krakatau (6 Sep 2026) | Sunda Strait (between Java and Sumatra), Indonesia | "Child of Krakatau", rose from the caldera of the 1883 eruption (massive tsunamis); flights hit at Soekarno-Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma airports
[26 Oct 2026] M6.5 earthquake | Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands, Japan | About 800 km SE of Japan's main islands; ~30 volcanic islands; part of Tokyo; UNESCO Natural Heritage 2011; near Izu-Bonin-Mariana subduction zone
Aletsch Glacier | Switzerland | Largest and longest glacier in the Alps; valley glacier; part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO site
Philippines: Pacific Ring of Fire; other volcanoes Mayon, Taal, Pinatubo; capital Manila; currency Philippine Peso. Sunda Strait links the Java Sea with the Indian Ocean.
Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of remaining ice in 2026, second-highest after 2022 (GLAMOS, SCNAT); causes: low winter snowfall + record summer heatwaves.
## Siang Project Protests (27 Oct 2026)
Protests against the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, Arunachal Pradesh: clashes and arson in Pasighat; NHPC office and a police station attacked; concerns over displacement and the Siang ecosystem.
Brahmaputra = Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibet) = Siang (Arunachal); joins Dibang and Lohit in Assam. NHPC est. 1975, HQ Faridabad.
CWC glacial lake monitoring: the Central Water Commission monitors 2,843 glacial lakes and water bodies of the Himalayan region by satellite; its 2011-2025 study found many lakes expanding.
# Firsts, Gi Tags, Energy and Waste
## Firsts and Places
FIRST | Place / fact
First port-based e-methanol plant | Deendayal Port Authority, Gandhidham-Kandla, Gujarat (Gulf of Kutch; formerly Kandla Port); 150 tonnes/day
First plastic-free oil terminal | Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal (Mumbai Port Authority), during Swachhata Abhiyan-2026 (Gandhi Jayanti)
Uttarakhand's first real-time GLOF warning | Vasundhara Lake, Chamoli
First high-altitude snow leopard safari | Leh
First state-level Red List of Ecosystems | Kerala
World's first integrated air pollution analysis centre | AATAL, Delhi-NCR
E-methanol = renewable electricity + water + biogenic CO2; a green marine fuel.
## GI Tags
Product | State | Fact
Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad | Gujarat | Gram-flour sweet, prasad of Ambaji Temple (Banaskantha; Shakti Peetha); applied 1 Oct 2026 by Shri Arasuri Ambaji Mata Devasthan Trust; GI on 8 Oct 2026; certificate 11 Oct (first day of Sharadiya Navratri)
Mandar | Jharkhand | Folk percussion instrument; double-sided barrel drum of red clay and leather; Chotanagpur tribal culture; made at Jarjatta, Raidih block, Gumla
GI Act 1999, in force 15 Sep 2003; Registry Chennai (CGPDTM, DPIIT); valid 10 years, renewable; first GI: Darjeeling Tea (2004-05).
## Kalpasar Project
About 30-km dam across the Gulf of Khambhat (Gujarat); freshwater reservoir; irrigation for 10 lakh+ ha, mainly Saurashtra.
Two tripartite MoUs on 24 Sep 2026 at the 9th India International Water Week, New Delhi: CWC, Gujarat's Kalpasar Department, Deltares (Netherlands), Delft University of Technology.
CWC: est. 1945, HQ New Delhi, Ministry of Jal Shakti.
## E-Waste
Generated 13.98 lakh tonnes (2024-25) vs 12.54 lakh t (2023-24); India 3rd-largest generator after China and USA.
E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022: in force 1 Apr 2023; 106 categories incl. solar PV; EPR recycling target 70% (2025-26, 2026-27), 80% from 2027-28.
Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022: ban landfill and incineration of waste batteries.
Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016; India party to the Basel Convention.
## Energy and Geo-heritage Indices
State Energy Efficiency Index 2024 (6th edition): by BEE; Maharashtra topped; Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Tripura led their groups; 66 indicators, 36 States/UTs (AP angle).
IUGS geological heritage sites: Mawmluh Cave (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) is in the first 100 IUGS geological sites.
## Equal-Area World Maps
UNGA resolution promoting equal-area maps: moved by Togo ("Correct the Map"); 164 of 193 in favour incl. India; USA voted against.
Mercator projection (Gerardus Mercator, 1569) enlarges high latitudes; Africa is ~14 times larger than Greenland; useful for navigation (constant compass bearings are straight lines); no flat map keeps area, shape, distance and direction together.
The map change is only visual; borders and sovereignty are unaffected.
Kandla e-methanol plant: a joint project of Deendayal Port Authority and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL); capacity 150 tonnes per day; about ₹2,300 crore.

⚠ Black carbon is not a greenhouse gas — a particle that absorbs radiation; sulphate aerosols cool
Methane: ~80 times CO2 warming over 20 years; second-largest contributor after CO2
Stratospheric ozone ~10–50 km; tropospheric surface–10 km
Ozone causes loss of ~110 million tonnes staple crops/year; air pollution ~7 million premature deaths/year globally
## 2. India
Air pollution: 1.67 million deaths in 2019 (17.8%), loss US$36.8 billion (1.36% of GDP)
Residential fuels = ~60% of South Asia's black carbon; Indo-Gangetic Plain hotspot
Methane (2016, Third BUR): Agriculture 73.96%, Waste 14.46%, Energy 10.62%, Industry 0.96%
⚠ India has not joined the Global Methane Pledge — calls farm methane "survival emissions"
## 3. International framework
Kigali Amendment | 2016; India ratified Sept 2021; freeze HFCs by 2028, cut 85% by 2047; can avoid 0.5°C by 2100
Global Methane Pledge | COP26 Glasgow 2021; cut 30% from 2020 levels by 2030; 159 countries + EC
## 4. India's measures
Air Act 1981; NAAQS 2009 (12 pollutants); National AQI 2015; GRAP 2017 (Delhi-NCR)
NCAP: 130 cities, 24 States/UTs; 2025–26: 65 cities within PM2.5 limit 40 µg/m³; Delhi 102 µg/m³; only 14 met PM10 (60 µg/m³)

- AGREE: the notes clearly support the given key.
- CONFLICT: the notes clearly support a different option. Give that option's number in "option" and quote or closely paraphrase the deciding line of the notes in "evidence". - NOT_COVERED: the notes do not contain the fact needed, or the question is garbled/unanswerable as written (say which in evidence).

Rules: "option" is 1-based and 0 when there is no alternative option (AGREE / NOT_COVERED).
